# Haven Security & AI Audit — Working Tree (`feat/identity-foundation`)

Scope: `convex/`, `src/`, `ios/`, `graph/`, `scripts/`, config. Excluded per instructions: `node_modules`, `.claude`, `convex/_generated`, `.worktrees`, `.entire`. Also excluded `.superpowers/sdd/*.diff` (historical diffs, not current state). `.env.local` was never read; env var **names** come from `grep process.env` and `.env.local.example`.

---

# PART A — AI / EMBEDDINGS

## A1. Complete inventory of AI integrations

Every LLM/embedding call in the product lives in **one file**, `convex/openaiClient.ts` (329 lines), invoked only from Convex **actions**. There is no client-side inference on web or iOS.

| # | Feature | Entry point | Provider path | Model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Screenshot profile extraction (vision) | `convex/captures.ts:301` `extract` (internalAction) → `extractProfile` `openaiClient.ts:154` | `EXTRACTION_*` prefix, else OpenAI | `EXTRACTION_MODEL`, default `gpt-4o-mini` (`openaiClient.ts:122`) |
| 2 | "Ask my network" (multi-turn) | `convex/people.ts:2448` `ask` (public action) → `askNetwork` `openaiClient.ts:281` | `ASK_*` prefix, else OpenAI | `ASK_MODEL`, default `gpt-4o-mini` (`openaiClient.ts:129`) |
| 3 | Embeddings (people + memories) | `people.ts:1993` / `memories.ts:162` → `embedText` `openaiClient.ts:318` | **OpenAI only, hard-pinned** | `text-embedding-3-small`, 1536-dim (`openaiClient.ts:320`) |
| 4 | Local name-guessing (graph tool) | `graph/Sources/GraphCore/GuessEngine.swift:29` → `OllamaProvider.swift:37` | **localhost Ollama, no egress** | `llama3.2` default (`OllamaProvider.swift:31`) |

**Status: Implemented** for 1–4.

### Provider swapping and key handling — `openaiClient.ts:99-119`
`chatConfig(prefix, ...)` reads `<PREFIX>_BASE_URL` / `<PREFIX>_API_KEY` / `<PREFIX>_MODEL`. A custom base URL **must** bring its own key and model — `requireEnv` throws otherwise (`openaiClient.ts:116-117`). The comment states this is deliberate: falling back "would hand the OpenAI bearer to a third-party host". This is a **correctly-implemented credential-confusion guard**.

Embeddings deliberately **not** swappable (`openaiClient.ts:94-98`): the vector index is pinned to 1536 dims, so a provider change is a re-embed migration.

**Env var NAMES only** (no values read): `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `EXTRACTION_BASE_URL`, `EXTRACTION_API_KEY`, `EXTRACTION_MODEL`, `ASK_BASE_URL`, `ASK_API_KEY`, `ASK_MODEL`, `COMPOSIO_API_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `WAITLIST_FROM_EMAIL`, `CLERK_JWT_ISSUER_DOMAIN`, `EVAL_RUNS`; client-side `VITE_CONVEX_URL`, `VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS`, `VITE_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT`, `VITE_FEEDBACK_TOKEN`; `.env.local.example` additionally lists `DATABASE_URL`, `DIRECT_URL`.

**Which provider actually serves traffic: Configured-externally-not-verifiable.** `openaiClient.ts:96` states extraction is pointed at `interfaze.ai` "to spend credit there", but that is env-driven and unverifiable from the tree.

### Exact prompt texts

**Extraction prompt** — `openaiClient.ts:60-72` (single joined string):
> "This is a screenshot the user took of someone's social or professional profile. Identify which platform it is from (branding, layout, UI chrome) and extract the person's visible details. Only report what is actually visible; never guess a handle or invent text. If the image is not a person's profile, set is_profile to false. A field this platform does not have is null. Prefer null to a near miss."

The trailing sentence has a documented security rationale (`openaiClient.ts:66-70`): a mis-filled `headline` "makes a person findable by somebody else's account name" because headline feeds the keyword haystack and the embedding.

**Ask prompt** — `openaiClient.ts:263-276` (system role):
> "You are searching one person's private notes about people they know. / Each entry below is one person: a #number, their details, and dated lines the user wrote about them. / Answer only from these entries. Never invent a person, a fact, or a #number. / … Return a match as 'direct' when the person themselves fits the need. / Return 'bridge' when nobody fits directly but this person is a plausible route to someone who does (for example: they work at a startup accelerator, so they likely know founders). / A bridge must never be dressed up as a direct match, and its 'why' must say what the route is. / If the request is too vague to answer without guessing, return no matches and ask exactly one clarifying question. …"

**Graph guess prompt** — `graph/Sources/GraphCore/GuessPrompt.swift:14-42`, assembled from `"You are looking at message snippets exchanged with an unnamed contact, identified only by \(identifier)."` (or the group variant listing member names), plus `Me:` / `Them:` prefixed raw iMessage snippets.

### Structured output handling — **Implemented, strict**
- Extraction: `response_format: json_schema`, `strict: true`, `EXTRACTION_SCHEMA` at `openaiClient.ts:28-58` with `additionalProperties: false` and every property in `required` (nullable types express optionality per strict-mode rules).
- Ask: `ASK_SCHEMA` `openaiClient.ts:225-261`, same strictness.
- Both check `message.refusal` and throw on a non-string content (`openaiClient.ts:186-189`, `303-306`).
- Post-parse validation: extraction rejects `!is_profile` or empty name (`openaiClient.ts:200-202`); ask **re-validates every model-returned `ref`** against the `refs` array actually shown, drops repeats and out-of-enum `kind` (`people.ts:2540-2565`), and caps at `MAX_ASK_MATCHES = 10` (`people.ts:2211`).

### Retry / error handling
- **Embeddings: Implemented.** `EMBED_RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [30_000, 300_000]` (`people.ts:81`); `people.ts:1993-2018` reschedules itself, gives up after 3 attempts with `console.error`, never throws. Same pattern for memories at `memories.ts:162-190`.
- **Extraction: Partial (no automatic retry).** `captures.ts:301-333` catches and writes a failure row; retry is user-initiated via `retryExtract` (`captures.ts:581`). Errors are split: only two allowlisted strings reach the client, everything else (which can contain raw OpenAI response bodies and env-var hints) goes to `errorDetail` behind a generic message — `captures.ts:274-297`. **Verified not projected** to clients: `listCaptures` returns validator omits `errorDetail` (`captures.ts:336-349`).
- **Ask: Missing retry** — a provider failure surfaces to the caller.
- Backfills swallow per-row failures and continue (`people.ts:2606`, `memories.ts:226`).

## A2. Vector search

**Two `vectorIndex` definitions, both 1536-dim, both `userId`-filtered:**
- `convex/schema.ts:100-104` — `people.by_embedding`
- `convex/schema.ts:125-129` — `memories.by_embedding`

**Four `ctx.vectorSearch` call sites**, all inside actions, all with `filter: (q) => q.eq("userId", userId)` where `userId` is derived server-side by `requireUser`, never client-supplied:
- `people.ts:2105` + `people.ts:2110` — `semanticSearch` (limits: `SEMANTIC_RESULT_LIMIT = 8`, `MEMORY_CANDIDATE_LIMIT = 64`, floor `MIN_SEMANTIC_SCORE = 0.3` — `people.ts:49-56`)
- `people.ts:2381` + `people.ts:2386` — `rankPeopleForAsk`, deliberately without the score floor (`people.ts:2370-2373`)

**Embedding generation.** Input built by `buildEmbedText` (`src/lib.ts:319`): name, platform+handle, headline, bio, "role at company", city, and the user's free-text `context`. Sliced to `MAX_EMBED_INPUT_LENGTH = 8000` (`people.ts:73`, applied `people.ts:1980`). **Idempotency: Implemented** — `embeddedText` is the key; unchanged text skips the paid call (`people.ts:1982-1984`, `memories.ts:151-153`).

Scheduled on every write that touches context/fields: `captures.ts:183,452,561`; `people.ts:675,877,1309,1528,1735,1811`. Cron backfills every interval: `crons.ts:8-24` → `people.backfillEmbeddings`, `memories.backfillMemoryEmbeddings`.

**Deletion of source rows removes embeddings — Implemented.**
- `deletePerson` (`people.ts:1543-1568`) deletes storage blobs, `personHandles`, **`deleteMemories`**, ends the connection, then the person row. Embeddings live *on* those rows, so they go with them.
- `purgeAccountData`/`purgeOwnedRows` (`profiles.ts:680-815`) does the same per page, explicitly calling `deleteMemories` with the comment that omitting it would leave rows "still sitting in the vector index" (`profiles.ts:715-718`).

**Stale-embedding risk — one real gap (by design, documented).** `syncMemories` is **additive only** (`memories.ts:48-51`): *"A note the user later edits away keeps its memory row… The cost is that a typo fixed in the note leaves the typo'd line searchable."* Consequence beyond typos: **a user who edits sensitive text out of a person's note does not remove it from semantic search or from the ask dossier** — the memory row and its embedding persist until the person is deleted. Cap `MAX_MEMORIES_PER_PERSON = 200` (`memories.ts:17`); once full, new lines are silently dropped (`memories.ts:70-73`). **Status: Implemented-as-specified / data-minimization gap.**

## A3. Chat / conversational AI — **Implemented (bounded multi-turn)**

`people.ts:2448` `ask` accepts `history: AskTurn[]` (oldest first). **Client owns the conversation; server keeps no session state** (`people.ts:2443-2446`, `2452-2454`). ## A4. `graph/` — **NOT purely deterministic**

The graph pipeline (identity resolution, roster building, acquaintance derivation) is deterministic — `AcquaintanceScoring.swift:5-17` is a table of hand-calibrated constants (`strongThreshold 1.0`, `likelyThreshold 0.2`, `coActiveDayWeight 0.1`, cap 5), no model.

**But there is an LLM path:** `graph-cli guess` (`graph/Sources/graph-cli/main.swift:574`, `:528` `let provider = OllamaProvider()`) runs `GuessEngine.run` over unnamed nodes. Properties:
- **Local-only, no egress**: `http://localhost:11434` default (`OllamaProvider.swift:29`), described in-file as "zero-cost, zero-data-leaves-the-machine provider per PLAN.md; a cloud provider is explicit opt-in and out of scope."
- **Explicit opt-in subcommand**, not part of the default build/json flow.
- Privacy hardening is deliberate and unusual: `URLSession(configuration: .ephemeral)` never `.shared`, because `.shared` has an on-disk `URLCache` — "exactly the kind of 'written to disk' path this step's privacy discipline forbids for message-derived text" (`OllamaProvider.swift:22-27`), plus `request.cachePolicy = .reloadIgnoringLocalAndRemoteCacheData` (`:43`).
- **Real iMessage message text is the prompt input.** `SnippetReader.swift:16-21` carries a LOUD NOTICE: it is "the ONLY file in the entire project allowed to SELECT message.text", read lazily per candidate and never persisted (`GuessEngine.swift:44-46`). Enforced by test `graph/Tests/GraphCoreTests/MessageTextNeverCarriedTests.swift`.
- Progress logging redacts: "Progress only, never the guessed name or any snippet text" (`main.swift:469-470`).

**Scripts.** `scripts/eval-ask.ts:1-14` is a hand-run live-provider eval (talks to the provider directly, never Convex, using prebuilt fixtures in `src/askFixtures.ts`) — **it does hit live provider APIs** when run.

## B2. Authorization — enumeration

I read every `export const` in `convex/*.ts` against its `requireUser`/`ctx.auth` line. Result:

**Public functions with NO identity verification — exactly two:**

| Function | Location | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| `profiles.getByHandle` | `convex/profiles.ts:1040-1054` | **Intentional and correctly scoped.** Backs the public web card a scanned beacon opens (`profiles.ts:1038-1039`: "Every field it returns is one a stranger may see"). Web caller: `src/CardPage.tsx:13`. **Status: Implemented (correct).** |
| `waitlist.joinWaitlist` | `convex/waitlist.ts:25-72` | **Intentional** — "these are strangers, not users" (`schema.ts:301`). Rate-limited first, validated server-side, deduped, and returns the same `"already"`/`"joined"` shape either way so it **never leaks whether an address was seen before** (`waitlist.ts:21-24`). **Status: Implemented (correct).** |

**Auth-required-but-non-throwing:** `stripe.hasProAccess` (`stripe.ts:67-84`) calls `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` directly and returns `false` when signed out rather than throwing — deliberate, it gates UI affordances (`stripe.ts:64-66`). `profiles.lookupByUsername` (`:1056`) *does* `requireUser` and returns only `{ username }`.

**Every other public `query`/`mutation`/`action` calls `requireUser` as its first statement** — verified line-adjacency for all of: `captures.ts:219,228,351,378,476,570,585`; `composio.ts:458,519,669,733`; `loveAlarm.ts:54,92,117,139,171`; `people.ts:724(add),961,979,1007,1036,1143,1265,1282,1343,1547,1621,2088,2475`; `profiles.ts:544,573,598,649,824,834,892,1000,1060,1099,1197`; `sharedNotes.ts:72,104`.

**Ownership-check pattern — confirmed consistent.** The canonical form is `requireUser` → fetch doc → compare doc's `userId` to the caller's `tokenIdentifier` → treat mismatch as not-found. E.g. `people.ts:1266-1269` (`getPerson`), `people.ts:1547-1551` (`deletePerson` throws `"Person not found"` on mismatch — no existence oracle). Internal functions document why they skip the check: `people.ts:2043-2044` — "internal-only, and the ids come from a vector search already filtered to the caller's userId."

**HTTP endpoints — one route, signature-verified.** `convex/http.ts:112-179` is the *only* `http.route`. It **fails closed** when `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (500, `:116-122`), requires a `stripe-signature` header (`:124-127`), verifies the **exact raw bytes** via `constructEventAsync` with a SubtleCrypto provider (`:131-141`) — comment correctly notes parse-then-reserialize would invalidate the signature — and re-validates every field after verification because "the signature proves Stripe sent it, not that it has the shape this code expects" (`http.ts:54-55`). Replay is covered by Stripe's timestamp tolerance (`:143-144`) plus a `lastEventCreated` monotonic guard in the schema (`schema.ts:337-341`). Subscriptions are webhook-write-only so "a compromised client cannot grant itself Pro" (`schema.ts:312-314`). **Status: Implemented (strong).**

## B3. Cross-tenant guards — **Implemented, currently present in the working tree**

`convex/handleKeys.ts` (modified in the working tree) contains **only pure string folding** — no Convex imports, no tenant logic (`handleKeys.ts:1-6`). The guards the question asks about live in `convex/people.ts`:

- **`oldestLiveOwner`** — `people.ts:346-397`. Three layers: (a) skip any row whose own `userId ≠ userId` with a **redacted** log (`:369-373`); (b) self-heal orphaned index rows by deleting them (`:381-384`); (c) **skip any row whose `personId` resolves to a different tenant's person** — "never leaked into the result, whatever wrote it that way" (`:385-390`). Tiebreak is on the **person doc's** `_creationTime`, not the index row's, because index rows are rewritten on every edit (`people.ts:340-345`).
- **`mergeHandleIntoOwner`** — `people.ts:476-524`. Before renaming a handle in place it re-asks `findHandleOwner` for the *new* valueKey and returns `{status: "refused", conflictingOwnerId}` if it belongs to someone else (`:494-503`).
- **`findHandleOwner`** — `people.ts:418-444`, both lookups (platformId-first, then valueKey) funnel through `oldestLiveOwner`.

**Log hygiene is explicit here**: `people.ts:352-353` — "platform + row ids only — never the valueKey or platformId a caller passed in, which on most platforms is the personal handle itself."

Regression coverage exists: `convex/people.test.ts:3519` (tiebreak on person age) and `:3576` ("findHandleOwner refuses to return a person owned by a different tenant").

## B10. Prompt-injection surface — **Missing (no mitigation), 3 live paths**

There is **no delimiter fencing, escaping, instruction-hierarchy marker, or output scanning** anywhere. Untrusted text is concatenated straight into prompts.

1. **Ask over captured third-party content (highest risk — injection is *not* self-inflicted).**
   Chain: a stranger's profile `bio`/`headline` → extracted by the vision model (`openaiClient.ts:52-56`) → stored in `people.bio`/`headline` (`schema.ts:31-34`) → concatenated into a dossier (`src/lib.ts:385-389`) → sent as the `"The network:\n\n${dossiers}"` user message (`openaiClient.ts:291`), directly abutting the system prompt. **An attacker who controls their own public bio can plant instructions that reach the LLM of anyone who screenshots them.** The user's own free-text notes flow the same way (`people.ts:2320-2325`).
2. **Vision extraction on attacker-controlled pixels.** `extractProfile` reads an arbitrary image; text rendered *in* the screenshot is model input (`captures.ts:312`). A crafted image can attempt to steer `name`/`handle`/`bio`.
3. **Multi-turn history.** Up to 20 client-supplied turns with `role: "user" | "assistant"` are spliced in unvalidated as to content (`openaiClient.ts:292`). A client can **forge assistant turns** — only length (`MAX_ASK_TEXT_LENGTH = 2000`) and count are checked (`people.ts:2497-2504`).

**What limits the blast radius (real, but partial):**
- Strict `json_schema` output means the model cannot emit arbitrary prose in arbitrary shape (`openaiClient.ts:295-298`).
- **Server-side ref validation**: every returned `ref` is checked against the `refs` array actually shown, duplicates dropped, `kind` enum-checked, and the rendered `name/company/role/city` come from **`network[ref-1]`, the server's own data — not from the model** (`people.ts:2540-2565`). So injection cannot fabricate a person.
- Vector search is `userId`-filtered, so injected text cannot pull in another tenant's data.
- The extraction prompt's anti-guessing clause (`openaiClient.ts:71`) blunts field-confusion.

**Residual:** `match.why` is a free-form model-authored string returned to the client and rendered in the iOS ask panel — the one field an injected instruction can fully control. No output sanitization exists on it.

## Cross-cutting notes

**Web security headers — Implemented** (`vercel.json:16-56`, tested by `src/contentSecurityPolicy.test.ts`). Main app: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`, and a real CSP with `default-src 'self'`, **no `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval` in `script-src`** (only `style-src` has `unsafe-inline`), `base-uri 'self'`, `form-action 'self'`. Allowlist: two Clerk origins, two Convex deployments (+wss), one convex.site, `img.clerk.com`, `challenges.cloudflare.com` in `frame-src` (Turnstile). `/demo-sky.html` gets a separate, looser-framing (`SAMEORIGIN`) but tighter-network (`connect-src 'self'`) policy. Minor gaps: no `object-src 'none'`, no `frame-ancestors` (covered by XFO for legacy but not for modern nested contexts).

**Universal links deliberately disabled** — `Haven.entitlements:4-16` documents that `com.apple.developer.associated-domains` is absent (free personal team) and `public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` still carries a **placeholder Team ID**, so scanned codes land in Safari. Not a vulnerability, but a scanned-beacon flow that silently degrades.

## Priority findings

1. **Missing data export** (`B8`) — no portability/subject-access flow exists anywhere. Highest compliance-risk gap.
2. **Prompt injection via third-party bio → ask dossier** (`B10.1`) — attacker-controlled text reaches an LLM prompt with no fencing; only `why` escapes the schema/ref validation.
3. **PII in logs** — `convex/waitlist.ts:87-100` writes strangers' raw email addresses to deployment logs on all four branches.
4. **Deleted notes stay searchable** (`A2`) — `syncMemories` is additive (`memories.ts:48-51`), so editing text out of a note does not remove its row or its embedding from vector search or ask dossiers.
5. **Global (not per-caller) waitlist rate limit** (`B7`) — `waitlist.ts:16`, one 40/min bucket for the entire world; trivially floodable into denial of legitimate signups.
6. **No file protection on App Group data** (`B4`) — `CaptureQueue.swift:189,202` and `DirectoryMirror.swift:167` write plaintext directory + screenshots with no `NSFileProtection` class.
7. **Real identities to Polygres** (`B9`) — `sync_polygres.py` pushes un-anonymized graph exports; `anonymize_graph.py` is not in that path.
8. **`subscriptions` survives account deletion** (`profiles.ts:790-797`) — defensible, but verify it is disclosed in the privacy policy; `src/SupportPage.tsx:70-76` does not mention it.

# Haven Security & AI Audit — Working Tree (`feat/identity-foundation`)

Scope: `convex/`, `src/`, `ios/`, `graph/`, `scripts/`, config. Excluded per instructions: `node_modules`, `.claude`, `convex/_generated`, `.worktrees`, `.entire`. Also excluded `.superpowers/sdd/*.diff` (historical diffs, not current state). `.env.local` was never read; env var **names** come from `grep process.env` and `.env.local.example`.

---

# PART A — AI / EMBEDDINGS

## A1. Complete inventory of AI integrations

Every LLM/embedding call in the product lives in **one file**, `convex/openaiClient.ts` (329 lines), invoked only from Convex **actions**. There is no client-side inference on web or iOS.

| # | Feature | Entry point | Provider path | Model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Screenshot profile extraction (vision) | `convex/captures.ts:301` `extract` (internalAction) → `extractProfile` `openaiClient.ts:154` | `EXTRACTION_*` prefix, else OpenAI | `EXTRACTION_MODEL`, default `gpt-4o-mini` (`openaiClient.ts:122`) |
| 2 | "Ask my network" (multi-turn) | `convex/people.ts:2448` `ask` (public action) → `askNetwork` `openaiClient.ts:281` | `ASK_*` prefix, else OpenAI | `ASK_MODEL`, default `gpt-4o-mini` (`openaiClient.ts:129`) |
| 3 | Embeddings (people + memories) | `people.ts:1993` / `memories.ts:162` → `embedText` `openaiClient.ts:318` | **OpenAI only, hard-pinned** | `text-embedding-3-small`, 1536-dim (`openaiClient.ts:320`) |
| 4 | Local name-guessing (graph tool) | `graph/Sources/GraphCore/GuessEngine.swift:29` → `OllamaProvider.swift:37` | **localhost Ollama, no egress** | `llama3.2` default (`OllamaProvider.swift:31`) |

**Status: Implemented** for 1–4.

### Provider swapping and key handling — `openaiClient.ts:99-119`
`chatConfig(prefix, ...)` reads `<PREFIX>_BASE_URL` / `<PREFIX>_API_KEY` / `<PREFIX>_MODEL`. A custom base URL **must** bring its own key and model — `requireEnv` throws otherwise (`openaiClient.ts:116-117`). The comment states this is deliberate: falling back "would hand the OpenAI bearer to a third-party host". This is a **correctly-implemented credential-confusion guard**.

Embeddings deliberately **not** swappable (`openaiClient.ts:94-98`): the vector index is pinned to 1536 dims, so a provider change is a re-embed migration.

**Env var NAMES only** (no values read): `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `EXTRACTION_BASE_URL`, `EXTRACTION_API_KEY`, `EXTRACTION_MODEL`, `ASK_BASE_URL`, `ASK_API_KEY`, `ASK_MODEL`, `COMPOSIO_API_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `WAITLIST_FROM_EMAIL`, `CLERK_JWT_ISSUER_DOMAIN`, `EVAL_RUNS`; client-side `VITE_CONVEX_URL`, `VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS`, `VITE_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT`, `VITE_FEEDBACK_TOKEN`; `.env.local.example` additionally lists `DATABASE_URL`, `DIRECT_URL`.

**Which provider actually serves traffic: Configured-externally-not-verifiable.** `openaiClient.ts:96` states extraction is pointed at `interfaze.ai` "to spend credit there", but that is env-driven and unverifiable from the tree.

### Exact prompt texts

**Extraction prompt** — `openaiClient.ts:60-72` (single joined string):
> "This is a screenshot the user took of someone's social or professional profile. Identify which platform it is from (branding, layout, UI chrome) and extract the person's visible details. Only report what is actually visible; never guess a handle or invent text. If the image is not a person's profile, set is_profile to false. A field this platform does not have is null. Prefer null to a near miss."

The trailing sentence has a documented security rationale (`openaiClient.ts:66-70`): a mis-filled `headline` "makes a person findable by somebody else's account name" because headline feeds the keyword haystack and the embedding.

**Ask prompt** — `openaiClient.ts:263-276` (system role):
> "You are searching one person's private notes about people they know. / Each entry below is one person: a #number, their details, and dated lines the user wrote about them. / Answer only from these entries. Never invent a person, a fact, or a #number. / … Return a match as 'direct' when the person themselves fits the need. / Return 'bridge' when nobody fits directly but this person is a plausible route to someone who does (for example: they work at a startup accelerator, so they likely know founders). / A bridge must never be dressed up as a direct match, and its 'why' must say what the route is. / If the request is too vague to answer without guessing, return no matches and ask exactly one clarifying question. …"

**Graph guess prompt** — `graph/Sources/GraphCore/GuessPrompt.swift:14-42`, assembled from `"You are looking at message snippets exchanged with an unnamed contact, identified only by \(identifier)."` (or the group variant listing member names), plus `Me:` / `Them:` prefixed raw iMessage snippets.

### Structured output handling — **Implemented, strict**
- Extraction: `response_format: json_schema`, `strict: true`, `EXTRACTION_SCHEMA` at `openaiClient.ts:28-58` with `additionalProperties: false` and every property in `required` (nullable types express optionality per strict-mode rules).
- Ask: `ASK_SCHEMA` `openaiClient.ts:225-261`, same strictness.
- Both check `message.refusal` and throw on a non-string content (`openaiClient.ts:186-189`, `303-306`).
- Post-parse validation: extraction rejects `!is_profile` or empty name (`openaiClient.ts:200-202`); ask **re-validates every model-returned `ref`** against the `refs` array actually shown, drops repeats and out-of-enum `kind` (`people.ts:2540-2565`), and caps at `MAX_ASK_MATCHES = 10` (`people.ts:2211`).

### Retry / error handling
- **Embeddings: Implemented.** `EMBED_RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [30_000, 300_000]` (`people.ts:81`); `people.ts:1993-2018` reschedules itself, gives up after 3 attempts with `console.error`, never throws. Same pattern for memories at `memories.ts:162-190`.
- **Extraction: Partial (no automatic retry).** `captures.ts:301-333` catches and writes a failure row; retry is user-initiated via `retryExtract` (`captures.ts:581`). Errors are split: only two allowlisted strings reach the client, everything else (which can contain raw OpenAI response bodies and env-var hints) goes to `errorDetail` behind a generic message — `captures.ts:274-297`. **Verified not projected** to clients: `listCaptures` returns validator omits `errorDetail` (`captures.ts:336-349`).
- **Ask: Missing retry** — a provider failure surfaces to the caller.
- Backfills swallow per-row failures and continue (`people.ts:2606`, `memories.ts:226`).

## A2. Vector search

**Two `vectorIndex` definitions, both 1536-dim, both `userId`-filtered:**
- `convex/schema.ts:100-104` — `people.by_embedding`
- `convex/schema.ts:125-129` — `memories.by_embedding`

**Four `ctx.vectorSearch` call sites**, all inside actions, all with `filter: (q) => q.eq("userId", userId)` where `userId` is derived server-side by `requireUser`, never client-supplied:
- `people.ts:2105` + `people.ts:2110` — `semanticSearch` (limits: `SEMANTIC_RESULT_LIMIT = 8`, `MEMORY_CANDIDATE_LIMIT = 64`, floor `MIN_SEMANTIC_SCORE = 0.3` — `people.ts:49-56`)
- `people.ts:2381` + `people.ts:2386` — `rankPeopleForAsk`, deliberately without the score floor (`people.ts:2370-2373`)

**Embedding generation.** Input built by `buildEmbedText` (`src/lib.ts:319`): name, platform+handle, headline, bio, "role at company", city, and the user's free-text `context`. Sliced to `MAX_EMBED_INPUT_LENGTH = 8000` (`people.ts:73`, applied `people.ts:1980`). **Idempotency: Implemented** — `embeddedText` is the key; unchanged text skips the paid call (`people.ts:1982-1984`, `memories.ts:151-153`).

Scheduled on every write that touches context/fields: `captures.ts:183,452,561`; `people.ts:675,877,1309,1528,1735,1811`. Cron backfills every interval: `crons.ts:8-24` → `people.backfillEmbeddings`, `memories.backfillMemoryEmbeddings`.

**Deletion of source rows removes embeddings — Implemented.**
- `deletePerson` (`people.ts:1543-1568`) deletes storage blobs, `personHandles`, **`deleteMemories`**, ends the connection, then the person row. Embeddings live *on* those rows, so they go with them.
- `purgeAccountData`/`purgeOwnedRows` (`profiles.ts:680-815`) does the same per page, explicitly calling `deleteMemories` with the comment that omitting it would leave rows "still sitting in the vector index" (`profiles.ts:715-718`).

**Stale-embedding risk — one real gap (by design, documented).** `syncMemories` is **additive only** (`memories.ts:48-51`): *"A note the user later edits away keeps its memory row… The cost is that a typo fixed in the note leaves the typo'd line searchable."* Consequence beyond typos: **a user who edits sensitive text out of a person's note does not remove it from semantic search or from the ask dossier** — the memory row and its embedding persist until the person is deleted. Cap `MAX_MEMORIES_PER_PERSON = 200` (`memories.ts:17`); once full, new lines are silently dropped (`memories.ts:70-73`). **Status: Implemented-as-specified / data-minimization gap.**

## A3. Chat / conversational AI — **Implemented (bounded multi-turn)**

`people.ts:2448` `ask` accepts `history: AskTurn[]` (oldest first). **Client owns the conversation; server keeps no session state** (`people.ts:2443-2446`, `2452-2454`). Bounds: `MAX_ASK_HISTORY_TURNS = 20` (`people.ts:2217`), `MAX_ASK_TEXT_LENGTH = 2000` per turn (`people.ts:2216`), `ASK_NETWORK_LIMIT = 200` people, `ASK_MEMORIES_PER_PERSON = 12`, `MAX_DOSSIER_CHARS = 120_000` (`people.ts:2194-2207`).

UI: **iOS** `ios/Haven/Search/AskModel.swift:112` (`ask`), `:104-107` (arguments incl. history), `:144` `convex.action("people:ask")`, rendered by `ios/Haven/Search/AskPanel.swift`; screenshot `ios/.screens/gallery/15-ask-panel.png`. Tests: `ios/HavenTests/AskModelTests.swift`, `convex/ask.test.ts`. **No web ask UI found** — `src/` has no `api.people.ask` caller. Status: **Implemented (iOS), Missing (web)**.

Retrieval strategy is notable: the whole network goes in one call; vector retrieval only kicks in when the network hit the 200-person cap or the char budget truncated (`people.ts:2506-2519`).

## A4. `graph/` — **NOT purely deterministic**

The graph pipeline (identity resolution, roster building, acquaintance derivation) is deterministic — `AcquaintanceScoring.swift:5-17` is a table of hand-calibrated constants (`strongThreshold 1.0`, `likelyThreshold 0.2`, `coActiveDayWeight 0.1`, cap 5), no model.

**But there is an LLM path:** `graph-cli guess` (`graph/Sources/graph-cli/main.swift:574`, `:528` `let provider = OllamaProvider()`) runs `GuessEngine.run` over unnamed nodes. Properties:
- **Local-only, no egress**: `http://localhost:11434` default (`OllamaProvider.swift:29`), described in-file as "zero-cost, zero-data-leaves-the-machine provider per PLAN.md; a cloud provider is explicit opt-in and out of scope."
- **Explicit opt-in subcommand**, not part of the default build/json flow.
- Privacy hardening is deliberate and unusual: `URLSession(configuration: .ephemeral)` never `.shared`, because `.shared` has an on-disk `URLCache` — "exactly the kind of 'written to disk' path this step's privacy discipline forbids for message-derived text" (`OllamaProvider.swift:22-27`), plus `request.cachePolicy = .reloadIgnoringLocalAndRemoteCacheData` (`:43`).
- **Real iMessage message text is the prompt input.** `SnippetReader.swift:16-21` carries a LOUD NOTICE: it is "the ONLY file in the entire project allowed to SELECT message.text", read lazily per candidate and never persisted (`GuessEngine.swift:44-46`). Enforced by test `graph/Tests/GraphCoreTests/MessageTextNeverCarriedTests.swift`.
- Progress logging redacts: "Progress only, never the guessed name or any snippet text" (`main.swift:469-470`).

**Scripts.** `scripts/eval-ask.ts:1-14` is a hand-run live-provider eval (talks to the provider directly, never Convex, using prebuilt fixtures in `src/askFixtures.ts`) — **it does hit live provider APIs** when run.

---

# PART B — PRIVACY / SECURITY

## B1. Authentication (Clerk) — **Implemented across three surfaces**

- **Convex**: `convex/auth.config.ts:19-27`, provider `domain: CLERK_JWT_ISSUER_DOMAIN`, `applicationID: "convex"`. A missing env var now **throws with an actionable message** rather than silently resolving to `domain: undefined` (`auth.config.ts:8-17`). Tested: `convex/auth.config.test.ts`.
- **Web**: `src/main.tsx:16-30` — `<ClerkProvider>` wrapping `<ConvexProviderWithClerk>`, with `clerkUrlProps` from `src/clerkConfig.ts:38-41` and hash routing (`clerkConfig.ts:47`). The extensive comment (`clerkConfig.ts:1-35`) documents a production-only Account-Portal redirect loop and applies belt-and-braces fixes.
- **iOS**: `ios/Haven/HavenConvexAuthProvider.swift` — a Haven-owned fork of `ClerkConvexAuthProvider` whose one change is fetching the **`"convex"` JWT template token** (`:33`, `:87`) instead of the default session token, so the `aud` claim matches `applicationID`. Refresh path re-fetches the templated token (`:99-104`), since Clerk sessions expire ~60s.

Ownership key everywhere is `identity.tokenIdentifier` (`"issuer|subject"`), not the bare `subject` — `convex/authz.ts:9-17`. This is the stricter of the two options.

## B2. Authorization — enumeration

I read every `export const` in `convex/*.ts` against its `requireUser`/`ctx.auth` line. Result:

**Public functions with NO identity verification — exactly two:**

| Function | Location | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| `profiles.getByHandle` | `convex/profiles.ts:1040-1054` | **Intentional and correctly scoped.** Backs the public web card a scanned beacon opens (`profiles.ts:1038-1039`: "Every field it returns is one a stranger may see"). Returns `publicCardValidator` (`profiles.ts:85-95`) = `handle, name, photoUrl, city, handles, primaryPlatform` — **`userId` is not projected**. Input is normalized and `HANDLE_PATTERN`-gated before any DB read (`:1044-1047`), so it cannot be used as an arbitrary-key probe. Web caller: `src/CardPage.tsx:13`. **Status: Implemented (correct).** |
| `waitlist.joinWaitlist` | `convex/waitlist.ts:25-72` | **Intentional** — "these are strangers, not users" (`schema.ts:301`). Rate-limited first, validated server-side, deduped, and returns the same `"already"`/`"joined"` shape either way so it **never leaks whether an address was seen before** (`waitlist.ts:21-24`). **Status: Implemented (correct).** |

**Auth-required-but-non-throwing:** `stripe.hasProAccess` (`stripe.ts:67-84`) calls `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` directly and returns `false` when signed out rather than throwing — deliberate, it gates UI affordances (`stripe.ts:64-66`). `profiles.lookupByUsername` (`:1056`) *does* `requireUser` and returns only `{ username }`.

**Every other public `query`/`mutation`/`action` calls `requireUser` as its first statement** — verified line-adjacency for all of: `captures.ts:219,228,351,378,476,570,585`; `composio.ts:458,519,669,733`; `loveAlarm.ts:54,92,117,139,171`; `people.ts:724(add),961,979,1007,1036,1143,1265,1282,1343,1547,1621,2088,2475`; `profiles.ts:544,573,598,649,824,834,892,1000,1060,1099,1197`; `sharedNotes.ts:72,104`.

**Ownership-check pattern — confirmed consistent.** The canonical form is `requireUser` → fetch doc → compare doc's `userId` to the caller's `tokenIdentifier` → treat mismatch as not-found. E.g. `people.ts:1266-1269` (`getPerson`), `people.ts:1547-1551` (`deletePerson` throws `"Person not found"` on mismatch — no existence oracle). Internal functions document why they skip the check: `people.ts:2043-2044` — "internal-only, and the ids come from a vector search already filtered to the caller's userId."

**HTTP endpoints — one route, signature-verified.** `convex/http.ts:112-179` is the *only* `http.route`. It **fails closed** when `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (500, `:116-122`), requires a `stripe-signature` header (`:124-127`), verifies the **exact raw bytes** via `constructEventAsync` with a SubtleCrypto provider (`:131-141`) — comment correctly notes parse-then-reserialize would invalidate the signature — and re-validates every field after verification because "the signature proves Stripe sent it, not that it has the shape this code expects" (`http.ts:54-55`). Replay is covered by Stripe's timestamp tolerance (`:143-144`) plus a `lastEventCreated` monotonic guard in the schema (`schema.ts:337-341`). Subscriptions are webhook-write-only so "a compromised client cannot grant itself Pro" (`schema.ts:312-314`). **Status: Implemented (strong).**

## B3. Cross-tenant guards — **Implemented, currently present in the working tree**

`convex/handleKeys.ts` (modified in the working tree) contains **only pure string folding** — no Convex imports, no tenant logic (`handleKeys.ts:1-6`). The guards the question asks about live in `convex/people.ts`:

- **`oldestLiveOwner`** — `people.ts:346-397`. Three layers: (a) skip any row whose own `userId ≠ userId` with a **redacted** log (`:369-373`); (b) self-heal orphaned index rows by deleting them (`:381-384`); (c) **skip any row whose `personId` resolves to a different tenant's person** — "never leaked into the result, whatever wrote it that way" (`:385-390`). Tiebreak is on the **person doc's** `_creationTime`, not the index row's, because index rows are rewritten on every edit (`people.ts:340-345`).
- **`mergeHandleIntoOwner`** — `people.ts:476-524`. Before renaming a handle in place it re-asks `findHandleOwner` for the *new* valueKey and returns `{status: "refused", conflictingOwnerId}` if it belongs to someone else (`:494-503`).
- **`findHandleOwner`** — `people.ts:418-444`, both lookups (platformId-first, then valueKey) funnel through `oldestLiveOwner`.

**Log hygiene is explicit here**: `people.ts:352-353` — "platform + row ids only — never the valueKey or platformId a caller passed in, which on most platforms is the personal handle itself."

Regression coverage exists: `convex/people.test.ts:3519` (tiebreak on person age) and `:3576` ("findHandleOwner refuses to return a person owned by a different tenant").

## B4. Encryption

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Client-side / end-to-end encryption | **Missing.** No CryptoKit, no `SecKey`, no envelope encryption anywhere in `ios/`, `src/`, or `convex/`. All notes, handles, phone numbers and screenshots are plaintext-at-rest in Convex, readable by the operator. |
| Secure Enclave | **Missing.** Zero hits for `SecureEnclave`, `kSecAttrTokenID`, `LAContext` across `ios/`. No biometric gate on the app. |
| iOS Keychain (own code) | **Missing (delegated).** Only two hits repo-wide: a comment at `ios/Haven/HavenApp.swift:44` and the `keychain-access-groups` entitlement `ios/Haven/Haven.entitlements:17-20` (`$(AppIdentifierPrefix)com.inhavens.haven`). **Haven writes nothing to the Keychain itself** — session tokens are stored by the Clerk SDK. *What exactly is stored there is not verifiable from this tree* → **Configured-externally-not-verifiable**. |
| App Group at-rest data | **Partial — plaintext, no file-protection class set.** `ios/Haven/Shared/HavenAppGroup.swift:14` group `group.com.inhavens.haven`, held by both app (`Haven.entitlements:31-34`) and share extension (`HavenShare.entitlements`). `CaptureQueue.swift:189` writes `JSONEncoder` output with `options: .atomic` — **no `.completeFileProtection`** — plus raw screenshot images at `:202`. `DirectoryMirror.swift:167` writes the whole cached directory (names, handles) the same way. **No `NSFileProtection*` / `FileProtectionType` anywhere in `ios/`.** Files inherit the default `NSFileProtectionCompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication`, so cached directory + captured screenshots are readable after first unlock without any additional gate. |

## B5. Logging / PII leakage

**Convex — one confirmed PII leak:**

- **`convex/waitlist.ts:87-100`** — logs **raw email addresses** on all four paths: `console.log("Waitlist confirmation sent to ${args.email} …")`, `console.warn(… ${args.email}: ${result.reason})`, `console.error(… ${args.email}: ${result.error})`, and `console.error("Waitlist confirmation threw for ${args.email}:", err)`. Every public waitlist signup writes a stranger's email into Convex deployment logs (and any downstream log sink). **Status: Missing (redaction).** This is the only place PII reaches a log statement.

Every other convex log is **id-only and deliberately redacted**: `people.ts:355,371,387` (platform + row `_id`s only, per the explicit comment at `:352`), `people.ts:1920` (owner/target ids), `people.ts:2005` / `2606`, `memories.ts:175` / `226` (memory ids), `composio.ts:800`/`814` (Clerk `userId` + Composio account id — pseudonymous ids, not names), `http.ts:95,120,145,163` (Stripe event/subscription ids).

**iOS — clean.** Only two logging sites exist repo-wide:
- `ios/Haven/LaunchLog.swift:54-55` — `logger.info("\(milestone, privacy: .public): +\(elapsedMs…, privacy: .public)ms")` — milestone name + timing only.
- `ios/Haven/Capture/CaptureDrain.swift:196` — `logger.notice("handle dropped at the 8-handle cap: \(platform, privacy: .public)")` — **platform name only, never the handle value**.

No `print(`, no `NSLog` in shipping iOS code. Correct use of `privacy:` annotations on both. **Status: Implemented.**

## B6. Analytics / crash reporting — **Missing (deliberate)**

Zero PostHog / Sentry / Firebase / Crashlytics / Amplitude / Mixpanel / Segment / Datadog / Bugsnag / GA across `src/`, `ios/`, `convex/`, `index.html`, `package.json`. (The only `segment` matches are `src/lib.ts` URL-path parsing.) Corroborated by `ios/Haven/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`: `NSPrivacyTracking: false`, `NSPrivacyTrackingDomains: []` (empty array), and the sole required-reason API declared is `UserDefaults` with reason `CA92.1` ("this app's own data only") for two local flags.

**One third-party widget exists, admin-gated:** `src/FeedbackWidget.tsx:14-27` dynamically imports `feedback-sdk-widget` and renders `<feedback-widget endpoint token>` **only when `useIsAdmin()` is true** *and* both `VITE_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT`/`VITE_FEEDBACK_TOKEN` are set. Admin allowlist is `import.meta.env.VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS` (`src/useIsAdmin.ts`). Note: the CSP `connect-src` (below) does **not** allowlist any feedback origin, so this only functions against a same-origin endpoint. **Status: Implemented (admin-only, not general analytics).**

## B7. Rate limiting — **Implemented, broad; one structural weakness**

Mechanism: `convex/rateLimit.ts:14-55`, a **fixed-window** counter in the `rateLimits` table keyed `(userId, action)`. Documented trade-off (`rateLimit.ts:6-9`): a caller at a window boundary can burst to **2× max**, accepted for a denial-of-wallet threat model. Actions run in mutations; actions reach it through `internal.people.enforceRateLimit` (`people.ts:2070-2082`), whose `userId` is "the caller's own identity, derived server-side… not a client-supplied authorization key" (`:2066-2069`).

Complete window inventory:

| Action | Cap | Window | Cite |
|---|---|---|---|
| `joinWaitlist` | **40 (GLOBAL)** | 1 min | `waitlist.ts:14,35-41` |
| `createCapture` | 10 / 100 | min / day | `captures.ts:231-232` |
| `retryExtract` | 10 / 100 | min / day | `captures.ts:588-589` |
| `acceptManual` | 30 | min | `captures.ts:480` |
| `semanticSearch` | 30 | min | `people.ts:2089-2093` |
| **`ask`** | **10 / 100** | **min / day** | `people.ts:2478-2490` |
| `addPerson` | 30 | min | `people.ts:724` |
| `updatePerson` / `editPerson` | 60 / 60 | min | `people.ts:1283`, `1344` |
| `saveSharedProfile` | 30 | min | `people.ts:1622` |
| `updateSharedNote` | 60 | min | `sharedNotes.ts:105` |
| `profiles:generateUploadUrl` | 10 | min | `profiles.ts:574-580` |
| `recordOnboardingStep` / `updateMyProfile` | 60 | min | `profiles.ts:599`, `893` |
| `setUsername` / `claimHandle` | 10 | min | `profiles.ts:835`, `1001` |
| `connect` / `disconnect` | 20 | min | `profiles.ts:1100`, `1198` |
| `loveAlarm:startPresence` / `:heartbeat` | 20 / 120 | min | `loveAlarm.ts:55`, `93` |
| **Composio** `initiateSocialConnection` | 10 | min | `composio.ts:463-467` |
| `completeSocialConnection` | 40 | min | `composio.ts:527-531` |
| `resolveXPlatformId` / `resolveXUsername` | 10 each | min | `composio.ts:674-678`, `734-738` |
| **`xLookup:day` (shared daily cap)** | **50** | day | `composio.ts:590`, `680-684`, `740-744` |

**The `ask` double-window is the right shape** — the comment at `people.ts:2476-2478` states an ask costs ~100× a semantic search, so a burst limit alone would not bound a day's spend.

**Weakness — waitlist is a single GLOBAL counter, not per-caller.** `RATE_SENTINEL = "public:waitlist"` (`waitlist.ts:16`) means all signups worldwide share one 40/min bucket. The file is honest about it (`waitlist.ts:9-13`): there is no per-user key on an unauthenticated endpoint, and "a genuine burst past the cap is briefly turned away, acceptable for a private-beta waitlist." **Consequence: a trivial script can hold the public waitlist at capacity and deny real signups** — availability, not confidentiality. No IP-based limiting exists. **Status: Partial.**

Also note `purgeOwnedRows` clears `rateLimits` **last**, specifically so a purge cannot lift the caller's own caps mid-run (`profiles.ts:799-801`) — a well-considered ordering detail.

## B8. Account deletion and data export

**Deletion — Implemented end-to-end.**

Backend: `profiles.deleteMyAccount` (`profiles.ts:645-673`) → deletes profile + photo blob → `purgeOwnedRows` → schedules `internal.composio.deleteConnectedAccountsForUser`. Paginated continuation `purgeAccountData` (`profiles.ts:680-690`) is **guarded on the profile row being absent**, so a user who signs back in mid-purge doesn't get their *new* account emptied (`:674-679`).

`purgeOwnedRows` (`profiles.ts:693-815`, `PURGE_PAGE = 200`) covers: `people` (+ screenshot blob, photo blob, `personHandles`, **`memories`**), `captures` (+ blobs), rows in *other* directories pointing at the leaver (collapsed to frozen snapshots via `havenContactUserId: undefined, connectionEndedAt` — `:773-786`), both sides of `connections` + their `sharedNotes`, `loveAlarmPresence`, and finally `rateLimits`; reschedules itself if any table still has a full page.

**One table deliberately survives**: `subscriptions` (`profiles.ts:790-797`) — billing record retention, reasoned in-file. This is a defensible legal-basis retention but **should be disclosed in the privacy policy**; the SupportPage copy (`src/SupportPage.tsx:70-76`) enumerates what is removed and does not mention it.

Third-party cleanup: `composio.deleteConnectedAccountsForUser` (`composio.ts:777-820`) lists **all** connected accounts with no `statuses` filter — "an EXPIRED or INACTIVE connection still holds whatever token it last had" (`:795-797`) — and deletes each with `revoke_on_delete=true`.

UI: **iOS** `ios/Haven/Card/MyCardScreen.swift:97` → `MyCardModel.deleteAccount()` (`MyCardModel.swift:145-159`), which calls `profiles:deleteMyAccount` **then** `Clerk.shared.user?.delete()`. The ordering rationale is correct and documented (`MyCardModel.swift:135-144`): the purge needs a live token, so deleting the Clerk identity first would strand every row; the only bad outcome is an identity with nothing behind it, and the mutation is idempotent. Cites App Store guideline 5.1.1(v). Web: `src/SupportPage.tsx:62-70` documents the flow but offers no web button. **Status: Implemented (iOS + backend); web UI Missing.**

**Data export — Missing.** No `gdpr`, `takeout`, `dataExport`, `downloadMyData`, or archive-download function exists in `convex/`, `src/`, or `ios/`. (`ios/Haven/Shared/VCardContact.swift` + `VCardContactTests.swift` are *per-contact* vCard sharing — a share affordance, not a subject-access export.) This is the clearest GDPR/CCPA compliance gap: Art. 20 portability has no implementation.

## B9. Data sent to third parties

| Recipient | What leaves | Cite | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenAI** (or `EXTRACTION_*` host, e.g. interfaze.ai) | **A fetchable URL to the user's raw screenshot.** `ctx.storage.getUrl(capture.screenshotId)` is passed as `image_url.url` (`captures.ts:312`→`openaiClient.ts:170`), so the provider **fetches the image directly from Convex storage**. `detail: "low"` — chosen on measured cost/accuracy, `openaiClient.ts:165-169`. URL lifetime/auth is Convex-controlled and **not verifiable here**. | `captures.ts:311-315`, `openaiClient.ts:154-181` | Implemented |
| **OpenAI** (`ASK_*` host) | **The most sensitive payload in the system**: up to 200 dossiers × (name, role, company, city, platforms, headline, third-party bio, and up to 12 verbatim private notes each) — up to 120 KB per call — plus the query and up to 20 prior turns. | `people.ts:2523-2530`, `src/lib.ts:359-395` | Implemented |
| **OpenAI** (embeddings, hard-pinned) | Per person: name + platform/handle + headline + bio + role/company + city + **full free-text notes**, ≤8000 chars. Per memory: one note line verbatim. | `people.ts:1970-1985`, `memories.ts:154` | Implemented |
| **Composio** (`https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3`) | Clerk `tokenIdentifier` as `user_id` on every call (`composio.ts:387,496,553,615,640,797`), the toolkit slug, and **a saved person's X username** as a tool argument (`composio.ts:634-643`). Composio holds the OAuth tokens for connected LinkedIn/Instagram/X accounts. | `composio.ts:31,115` | Implemented |
| **Stripe** | Inbound webhooks only in this tree; `clerkUserId` must be stamped into `subscription_data[metadata]` by checkout (`http.ts:75-83`). No outbound Stripe API call exists in `convex/`. | `http.ts:11-14,112` | Partial |
| **Clerk** | Full auth: email, session, user id. Web `main.tsx:19`, iOS `HavenConvexAuthProvider.swift`, Convex `auth.config.ts`. | — | Implemented |
| **Resend** (`https://api.resend.com/emails`) | Waitlist signup **name + email address**. Skips silently if `RESEND_API_KEY`/`WAITLIST_FROM_EMAIL` unset. | `emailClient.ts:84-101`, `waitlist.ts:66-69` | Implemented |
| **Convex / Vercel** | Hosting + all data at rest + function logs (incl. the waitlist emails in B5). | `vercel.json`, `.vercel/project.json` | Implemented |
| **Apple** | StoreKit named as a future `subscriptions.source` but **not yet wired** (`schema.ts:325-329`). Contacts/Camera are on-device only — `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` explains the connect scanner "reads one code out of the frames and keeps none of them". | `schema.ts:326-328` | Planned |
| **Polygres (Postgres)** | ⚠️ `graph/scripts/sync_polygres.py` syncs `exports/graph.json` into `im_nodes`/`im_edges` — that export carries **real phone numbers, emails, chat GUIDs and display names**. `anonymize_graph.py` is a *separate* script for the demo sky, **not** part of the sync path. Env names `DATABASE_URL`/`DIRECT_URL`. Mitigation: the script "never prints row contents (names, identifiers): only counts". | `sync_polygres.py:1-40`, `anonymize_graph.py:1-27` | Implemented (dev tool) |
| **Ollama** | **Not egress** — `localhost:11434`, explicitly local-only. Listed for completeness. | `OllamaProvider.swift:29` | N/A |
| **Feedback widget vendor** | Admin-only; endpoint is env-configured and not CSP-allowlisted. | `FeedbackWidget.tsx:8-9` | Configured-externally-not-verifiable |

## B10. Prompt-injection surface — **Missing (no mitigation), 3 live paths**

There is **no delimiter fencing, escaping, instruction-hierarchy marker, or output scanning** anywhere. Untrusted text is concatenated straight into prompts.

1. **Ask over captured third-party content (highest risk — injection is *not* self-inflicted).**
   Chain: a stranger's profile `bio`/`headline` → extracted by the vision model (`openaiClient.ts:52-56`) → stored in `people.bio`/`headline` (`schema.ts:31-34`) → concatenated into a dossier (`src/lib.ts:385-389`) → sent as the `"The network:\n\n${dossiers}"` user message (`openaiClient.ts:291`), directly abutting the system prompt. **An attacker who controls their own public bio can plant instructions that reach the LLM of anyone who screenshots them.** The user's own free-text notes flow the same way (`people.ts:2320-2325`).
2. **Vision extraction on attacker-controlled pixels.** `extractProfile` reads an arbitrary image; text rendered *in* the screenshot is model input (`captures.ts:312`). A crafted image can attempt to steer `name`/`handle`/`bio`.
3. **Multi-turn history.** Up to 20 client-supplied turns with `role: "user" | "assistant"` are spliced in unvalidated as to content (`openaiClient.ts:292`). A client can **forge assistant turns** — only length (`MAX_ASK_TEXT_LENGTH = 2000`) and count are checked (`people.ts:2497-2504`).

**What limits the blast radius (real, but partial):**
- Strict `json_schema` output means the model cannot emit arbitrary prose in arbitrary shape (`openaiClient.ts:295-298`).
- **Server-side ref validation**: every returned `ref` is checked against the `refs` array actually shown, duplicates dropped, `kind` enum-checked, and the rendered `name/company/role/city` come from **`network[ref-1]`, the server's own data — not from the model** (`people.ts:2540-2565`). So injection cannot fabricate a person.
- Vector search is `userId`-filtered, so injected text cannot pull in another tenant's data.
- The extraction prompt's anti-guessing clause (`openaiClient.ts:71`) blunts field-confusion.

**Residual:** `match.why` is a free-form model-authored string returned to the client and rendered in the iOS ask panel — the one field an injected instruction can fully control. No output sanitization exists on it.

---

## Cross-cutting notes

**Web security headers — Implemented** (`vercel.json:16-56`, tested by `src/contentSecurityPolicy.test.ts`). Main app: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`, and a real CSP with `default-src 'self'`, **no `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval` in `script-src`** (only `style-src` has `unsafe-inline`), `base-uri 'self'`, `form-action 'self'`. Allowlist: two Clerk origins, two Convex deployments (+wss), one convex.site, `img.clerk.com`, `challenges.cloudflare.com` in `frame-src` (Turnstile). `/demo-sky.html` gets a separate, looser-framing (`SAMEORIGIN`) but tighter-network (`connect-src 'self'`) policy. Minor gaps: no `object-src 'none'`, no `frame-ancestors` (covered by XFO for legacy but not for modern nested contexts).

**Universal links deliberately disabled** — `Haven.entitlements:4-16` documents that `com.apple.developer.associated-domains` is absent (free personal team) and `public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` still carries a **placeholder Team ID**, so scanned codes land in Safari. Not a vulnerability, but a scanned-beacon flow that silently degrades.

## Priority findings

1. **Missing data export** (`B8`) — no portability/subject-access flow exists anywhere. Highest compliance-risk gap.
2. **Prompt injection via third-party bio → ask dossier** (`B10.1`) — attacker-controlled text reaches an LLM prompt with no fencing; only `why` escapes the schema/ref validation.
3. **PII in logs** — `convex/waitlist.ts:87-100` writes strangers' raw email addresses to deployment logs on all four branches.
4. **Deleted notes stay searchable** (`A2`) — `syncMemories` is additive (`memories.ts:48-51`), so editing text out of a note does not remove its row or its embedding from vector search or ask dossiers.
5. **Global (not per-caller) waitlist rate limit** (`B7`) — `waitlist.ts:16`, one 40/min bucket for the entire world; trivially floodable into denial of legitimate signups.
6. **No file protection on App Group data** (`B4`) — `CaptureQueue.swift:189,202` and `DirectoryMirror.swift:167` write plaintext directory + screenshots with no `NSFileProtection` class.
7. **Real identities to Polygres** (`B9`) — `sync_polygres.py` pushes un-anonymized graph exports; `anonymize_graph.py` is not in that path.
8. **`subscriptions` survives account deletion** (`profiles.ts:790-797`) — defensible, but verify it is disclosed in the privacy policy; `src/SupportPage.tsx:70-76` does not mention it.

# Haven iOS — Working-Tree Audit (`feat/identity-foundation`, uncommitted state)

Scope: `ios/` on the working tree as of 2026-08-05. ~7,000 lines of production Swift across 3 shipping targets + 1 test bundle. `ios/build/` and `ios/.screens/` are gitignored; `Haven.xcodeproj` is generated by XcodeGen from `project.yml` and is not tracked. 14 Swift source files and 10 test files are **untracked** (the whole `Haven/Contacts/` directory, `PlatformIdResolving`, `VCardContact`, `NameSuggestion`, `HandleStaleness`) — this audit treats them as current.

---

## 1. App structure

**Entry point.** `/Users/minhthiennguyen/Desktop/Euno/euno-app/ios/Haven/HavenApp.swift`
- `HavenApp: App` (`:22`), `@main`. Its `init` does nothing but `LaunchLog.markOnce` (`:28`).
- Module-level global `convex: ConvexClientWithAuth<String>` (`:11-19`), `@MainActor`, constructed with `HavenConvexAuthProvider(template: "convex")` against `Config.convexDeploymentUrl`.
- `LaunchGate` (`:56-80`) paints `LaunchBackground` (NightBackground + DustLayer, zero Clerk/Convex cost) then runs `Clerk.configure(publishableKey:)` in a `.task` and only then constructs `RootView`. Documented as a deliberate first-frame fix.

**Top-level routing.** `ios/Haven/RootView.swift:7`
- Switches on `AuthModel.authState` (`ios/Haven/AuthModel.swift:9-19`, a Combine mirror of `convex.authState`): `.loading → HavenLoadingScreen`, `.unauthenticated → WelcomeScreen`, `.authenticated → OnboardingFlow(userId:).id(userId)` (`RootView.swift:44-69`).
- Owns `CaptureSync` and triggers `captures.run()` on `.task` and on every `scenePhase == .active` (`:49-58`), and injects `\.requestCaptureDrain` into the environment (`:62-65`).
- Success haptic only on `signedOut → signedIn` (`:25`, `:85-87`).

**Post-onboarding shell.** `ios/Haven/HavenTabs.swift:8`
- Two tabs, two independent `NavigationStack` paths (`peopleRoute`, `searchRoute`, `:25-29`) — deliberately not shared so a person opened from search returns to search.
- People toolbar (`:166-209`): leading "More" menu listing `LegalDocument.allCases`; trailing scan (`qrcode.viewfinder`) → `ConnectScreen` sheet; trailing card (`person.crop.circle`) → `MyCardScreen`.
- `.onOpenURL` (`:99-121`) handles `haven://beacon` (widget → card, code side up) and `inhavens.com/<handle>` universal-link-shaped URLs via `ConnectAddress.handle(in:)`; a link to your own handle opens your own code instead of a self-connect.

**Screens.**

| Screen | File / symbol | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Welcome / sign-in | `Haven/Onboarding/WelcomeScreen.swift:12` | Wordmark, tagline, **Sign up** / **Sign in** → Clerk `AuthView` sheet (`:72-74`); privacy/terms links (`:81-98`) |
| Onboarding flow | `Haven/Onboarding/OnboardingFlow.swift:6` | Routes to the first unanswered question; owns the shared `Sky` |
| Q1 Name | `Haven/Onboarding/NameScreen.swift` | Required, not skippable |
| Q2 Location | `Haven/Onboarding/LocationScreen.swift` + `CityCompleter.swift:18` | MapKit `MKLocalSearchCompleter` typeahead filtered to `.locality`; skippable |
| Q3 Contact | `Haven/Onboarding/ContactScreen.swift:10` | Composio OAuth rows + typed fallback panels; skippable |
| Card reveal | `Haven/Card/CardRevealScreen.swift` | One-time moment; sky reseeded from the minted username (`OnboardingFlow.swift:61-71`, `RevealSky.seed`) |
| Directory ("People") | `Haven/Directory/DirectoryScreen.swift:9` | Paged people list, promo cards, contact suggestion, **Add someone** |
| Add Person | `Haven/Directory/AddPersonSheet.swift:14` | 3 required fields → queue → drain |
| Person | `Haven/Directory/PersonScreen.swift:12` | Reach rows, connection chip, the note (the point of the screen) |
| Person editor | `Haven/Directory/PersonEditor.swift:15` | Name/company/role/city/handles/photo, Disconnect, Delete |
| Search | `Haven/Search/SearchScreen.swift:10` | Live query + 3 facet chips + device-contact section + Ask panel |
| My Card | `Haven/Card/MyCardScreen.swift:12` | Card front/back (QR), 6 fields, address, **Sign out**, **Delete account**, Legal |
| Connect (scan) | `Haven/Connect/ConnectScreen.swift` + `ConnectModel.swift:74` | QR scan or typed address → public card → connect |
| Pin walkthrough | `Haven/Capture/PinWalkthrough.swift:16` | Teaches moving Haven to the front of the share sheet; hands over a real `ShareLink` |
| Lock Screen explainer | `Haven/Directory/LockScreenExplainer.swift` | Teaches adding the widget |
| Legal | `Haven/Legal/LegalSheet.swift`, `Haven/Model/LegalDocument.swift:12` | In-app `SafariPage` for privacy/terms |

**There is no Settings screen.** Account controls live on My Card (`MyCardScreen.swift:200-260`); legal is reachable from three places (Welcome, People toolbar menu, My Card).

**What a user can do end-to-end today (all implemented):** sign up/in → answer 3 onboarding questions (connect Instagram/X/LinkedIn via Composio, or type a handle/phone) → see their card revealed with a generated sky → add people by hand, by sharing a profile/screenshot/vCard from any app, by importing a device contact, or by scanning someone's Haven QR → write a note per person → search and ask over the directory → tap a handle to open Instagram/X/LinkedIn/Telegram/WhatsApp/tel: → edit or delete a person → edit their own card, claim a `@handle`, share their address, add a Lock Screen widget → sign out or delete their account.

---

## 2. Auth

**SDKs.** `project.yml:53-58` — `clerk-ios` from 1.3.0 (`ClerkKit` + `ClerkKitUI`), `clerk-convex-swift` pinned `exactVersion: 0.1.0`. The pinned ClerkConvex product is linked but its `ClerkConvexAuthProvider` is deliberately **not** used.

**Token handling.** `ios/Haven/HavenConvexAuthProvider.swift:19`
- A documented fork of `ClerkConvexAuthProvider` whose one change is fetching the **`"convex"` JWT template** token: `session.getToken(.init(template: template))` (`:80`). The stock provider's untemplated token carries the wrong audience and Convex silently hangs (`:1-17`).
- Refresh listener re-fetches the *templated* token on `.tokenRefreshed` (`:86-103`) — the event's own token is the default one.
- Session sync task maps Clerk `.sessionChanged` to `client.loginFromCache()` / `client.logout()` (`:105-138`).
- `logout()` cancels the refresh task and calls `Clerk.shared.auth.signOut()` (`:53-58`).

**Publishable keys.** `ios/Haven/Config.swift`
- `clerkDevelopmentKey` (`:24`) used in `#if DEBUG`; `clerkProductionKey` (`:73`) with a release-build `precondition` guarding against the placeholder (`:83-98`). Both are publishable client keys, not secrets; the file says so explicitly (`:33-36`).
- **Partial/unverified:** `Config.swift:56-61` states the production Clerk↔Convex pairing is "believed rather than verified" — nobody has signed in against production, and the production instance still needs its own `"convex"` JWT template.
- Deployment URLs split by build: dev `brilliant-puma-925`, prod `third-hound-186` (`:110-126`).

**Keychain.** No first-party keychain code exists — a grep for `kSec|SecItem|Keychain` across `Haven/` and `HavenShare/` returns only a prose mention in `HavenApp.swift:44`. The entitlement `keychain-access-groups = $(AppIdentifierPrefix)com.inhavens.haven` (`ios/Haven/Haven.entitlements:17-20`) exists **solely so the Clerk SDK can persist its device token**; `project.yml:107-109` documents that without it Clerk fails with OSStatus -34018 and sign-in returns 401. Contents are Clerk-SDK-owned. `HavenShare/HavenShare.entitlements` has **no** keychain group — the extension cannot read the session, by design (it does no network at all).

**Sign-out.** `MyCardModel.signOut()` (`ios/Haven/Card/MyCardModel.swift:174-177`): `try? Clerk.shared.auth.signOut()` then `LocalAccountState.clear()`. Confirmed call sites: the Sign-out alert (`MyCardScreen.swift:75-80`) and the post-deletion path (`MyCardScreen.swift:91-101`). The `try?` is documented as leaving a working retry rather than a lie (`MyCardModel.swift:168-173`).

**Account deletion — implemented.** `MyCardModel.deleteAccount()` (`:145-159`): `convex.mutation("profiles:deleteMyAccount")` **then** `Clerk.shared.user?.delete()`, in that order because the purge needs a live token; documented against App Store guideline 5.1.1(v) (`:131-144`). Bounded at 12s; failure surfaces a retryable message.

**Planned / regressed:** Sign in with Apple was **removed on 2026-08-04** (`WelcomeScreen.swift:47-53`) because the production Clerk plan caps social connections at three (Google, LinkedIn, X). The comment states guideline 4.8 requires it back **before App Store submission**. This is a shipping blocker recorded in a code comment only.

---

## 3. Backend calls

All Convex traffic goes through the single `convex` global. Reads go through `HavenNetwork.subscribe`.

**Queries (subscriptions)**

| Function | Call site | Live? |
|---|---|---|
| `people:listPeople` | `Directory/DirectoryModel.swift:135-136` | live |
| `people:listPeople` | `Capture/CaptureSync.swift:123-125` | `firstValueOnly: true` |
| `people:getPerson` | `Directory/PersonModel.swift:496-499` | live |
| `people:searchDirectory` | `Search/SearchModel.swift:178-181` | live, per-keystroke generation guard |
| `people:directoryFacets` | `Search/SearchModel.swift:189-192` | live |
| `profiles:getMyCard` | `Card/MyCardModel.swift:68-70` | live |
| `profiles:getMyCard` | `Card/MyNameModel.swift:35-37` | live (title only) |
| `profiles:getMyCard` | `Onboarding/OnboardingModel.swift:402-409` | `firstValueOnly: true` (device is sole writer during onboarding) |
| `profiles:getByHandle` | `Connect/ConnectModel.swift:175-180` | `firstValueOnly: true` |

**Mutations:** `people:saveSharedProfile` (`Capture/ConvexCaptureSink.swift:126`), `people:editPerson` (`Directory/PersonModel.swift:323, 349, 377`), `people:deletePerson` (`:459-461`), `captures:generateUploadUrl` / `captures:createCapture` (`ConvexCaptureSink.swift:69, 72`), `profiles:generateUploadUrl` (`MyCardModel.swift:100`, `PersonModel.swift:406`, `OnboardingModel.swift:321`), `profiles:updateMyProfile` (`MyCardModel.swift:84, 102`, `OnboardingModel.swift:323, 385`), `profiles:claimHandle` (`MyCardModel.swift:121`), `profiles:deleteMyAccount` (`:149`), `profiles:connect` (`ConnectModel.swift:155`), `profiles:disconnect` (`PersonModel.swift:432-433`), `profiles:recordOnboardingStep` (`OnboardingModel.swift:361-364`).

**Actions:** `people:ask` (`Search/AskModel.swift:144`), `composio:initiateSocialConnection` (`Onboarding/ContactConnector.swift:58-61`), `composio:completeSocialConnection` (`:88-91`), `composio:resolveXUsername` (`Capture/PlatformIdResolving.swift:127`).

**Not called:** `people:addPerson` exists server-side but is deliberately bypassed — `ConvexCaptureSink.swift:32-40` explains that `saveSharedProfile` is idempotent on `(platform, handle)`, which is what a replayable queued write needs.

**Subscription plumbing.** `ios/Haven/Model/HavenNetwork.swift`
- `HavenNetwork.deadline = 12` seconds (`:11`) — one number for the whole app, confirmed (not the 5s in `PlatformIdResolving`, which uses its own shorter `timeout`).
- `subscribe(to:with:yielding:firstValueOnly:onValue:onSilence:)` (`:38-61`). `firstValueOnly` uses `.first().timeout(...)`; otherwise `LiveSubscription.attach` (`:85-118`).
- `LiveSubscription` (`:67-118`) is the load-bearing fix: a bare Combine `.timeout` resets on every element, so a live subscription quiet for >12s used to **complete permanently** with no error. The watchdog now bounds only the *first* answer (`:92, :107-112`); pinned by `HavenTests/HavenNetworkTests.swift`.

**Pagination.** `DirectoryModel` (`Directory/DirectoryModel.swift:56-151`) grows a **window** rather than chaining cursors: `numItems: window` (starting 50, `:80`), `cursor: nil` always (`:132`). `loadMore()` (`:118-123`) adds another 50 and re-subscribes; triggered by the last row's `.onAppear` in a `LazyVStack` (`DirectoryScreen.swift:301-306`). `numItems` is a `Double` deliberately — `ConvexEncodable` wraps `Int` as `{"$integer":…}` which `v.number()` rejects (`:66-70`).

**DirectoryMirror** — `ios/Haven/Shared/DirectoryMirror.swift`
- Types: `MirrorHandle{platform, value}` (`:9`), `MirrorPerson{id, name, handles}` (`:42`), `DirectoryMirror{refreshedAt, people}` (`:56`).
- Stores **only** id/name/handles — no note, company, city or photo, documented at `:33-41`.
- Location: `<appGroupContainer>/directory-mirror.json` (`DirectoryMirrorStore.fileURL`, `:143-145`); ISO8601 JSON, `.atomic` write (`:163-168`), best-effort `load()` returning nil (`:175-178`), `clear()` (`:186-189`).
- Fallback when the App Group is unprovisioned: the app's own `Application Support/Haven/` (`:139-141`, `HavenAppGroup.appContainerURL:28-33`).
- Written by `CaptureSync.refreshMirror()` (`Capture/CaptureSync.swift:99-112`) from the first page of `people:listPeople` at `mirrorSize = 500` (`:150`), after **every** drain pass including empty ones.
- Read-side queries: `person(holding: ProfileLink)` / `(platform:value:)` (`:65-79`), `people(named:)` exact fold (`:86-90`), `search(_:limit:8)` substring (`:99-106`), and `nameSuggestions(for:limit:5)` fuzzy (`Shared/NameSuggestion.swift:74-96`, Levenshtein with a length-scaled threshold: 0 under 4 chars, 1 for 4–7, 2 for 8+, `:102-107`).
- `MirrorHandle.valueKey` / `indexKey` (`:24-30`) are documented ports of `convex/handleKeys.ts` — the dedup key must not drift.

**CaptureQueue** — `ios/Haven/Shared/CaptureQueue.swift`
- **One JSON file per capture**, `<container>/captures/<uuid>.json`, ISO8601 dates, `.atomic` writes (`:185-190`, `:263-265`). Rationale at `:108-116`: two processes writing one list file would clobber each other.
- Images copied (never referenced) into `<container>/captures/images/<uuid>.<ext>` (`:196-205`); `imageURL(named:)` hardens against `..` by taking only `lastPathComponent` (`:238-242`).
- `pending()` sorts oldest-first (replay order decides which person a note lands on) and **skips** undecodable files so one bad capture can't block the queue (`:217-231`).
- `forApp()` falls back to the private container; `drainable()` always includes the private container too, so captures written before the group was provisioned aren't stranded (`:141-160`).

**CaptureDrain** — `ios/Haven/Capture/CaptureDrain.swift:98-208`
- Per-item, independent `do/catch`; every call wrapped in `bounded { }` at 12s (`:187-193`) as a backstop over the sink's own bound, because `CaptureSync.isRunning` only resets when `run()` returns (`:101-111`).
- **Retry policy:** network failure → `kept` (never dropped). Missing screenshot file → `dropped` (retrying forever is worse). `status == "conflict"` **with** an `attachToPersonId` → exactly one resubmit with the attach stripped (`ConflictRetry.shouldRetry`, `:41-45`; applied at `:126-133` and `:146-152`), whatever that answers is final.
- `CaptureSync.run()` (`Capture/CaptureSync.swift:79-92`) guards re-entrancy, drains every queue, then refreshes the mirror.

## 4. Share extension (`HavenShare`)

**Accepted content.** `ios/HavenShare/Info.plist:85-100` — an `NSExtensionActivationRule` **predicate string** (not the dictionary form) using nested `SUBQUERY … .@count >= 1`:
- `public.url` AND NOT `public.file-url`
- `public.image` AND NOT `public.file-url`
- `public.plain-text` AND NOT `public.file-url`
- `public.vcard` (no file-url exclusion)

The 80-line comment (`:24-84`) records *why*: the dictionary form requires every attachment to be claimed, and Safari bundles page text + a snapshot ref + a plist alongside the URL, so the extension never appeared for a Safari share at all. `>= 1` ignores companions. Plain text is accepted because LinkedIn's app was verified on-device (2026-08-04) to share a profile as a sentence with the link inside it.

**Entry.** `HavenShare/ShareViewController.swift:10` — 60 lines. Reads `extensionContext?.inputItems`, presents `ShareSheet` in one of three states: `.ready(model, queue)`, `.unsupported`, `.unavailable` (no App Group). SwiftUI hosted in a `UIHostingController`.

**Parsing precedence.** `HavenShare/ShareInput.swift:15-65` — vCard → URL → plain text → image. vCard uses `loadDataRepresentation` (`:81-87`) and image uses the **callback** form of `loadFileRepresentation` (`:94-106`) because the system reclaims the temp file the moment the callback returns.

**Decisions.** `ios/Haven/Shared/ShareSheetModel.swift` (in `Shared/`, so the in-app pin walkthrough runs the same flow):
- `ShareSubject` (`:15-120`): `.profile(link:profileUrl:)`, `.screenshot(fileName:)`, `.contact(name:platform:handleValue:)`. Tracking params (`?s=`, `?igsh=`, `utm_*`) and trailing slashes stripped (`:101-106`); free-text shares try the whole message then each whitespace-separated word with trailing sentence punctuation stripped (`:59-74`, `:112-119`).
- vCard → phone preferred over email, nil if neither (`:87-96`); parsed by `Shared/VCardContact.swift:32-42` via `CNContactVCardSerialization`, reduced to name/first-phone/first-email only.
- `ShareSheetModel` (`:127-301`): `alreadyKnown` (exact handle hit in the mirror), `namePrefill` (LinkedIn slug guess or contact name only — never an Instagram/X handle, `:150-177`), `identityLine`, `nameMatches` (fuzzy for LinkedIn "link refresh", exact fold otherwise, `:216-223`), `canSave` (name non-empty), `capture(...)`.

**How data reaches the app.** The extension makes **zero network calls**. It writes a `QueuedCapture` into the App Group `captures/` directory and calls `completeRequest` (`ShareSheet.swift:208-216` — the sheet stays open on a failed write). The app drains it on next launch or foreground (`RootView.swift:49-58`). The extension reads the app's `directory-mirror.json` for its "already saved as…" and attach-to-person offers (`ShareViewController.swift:32`).

**Screenshot handling.** Image copied into the container at share time (`CaptureQueue.storeImage`), queued as `.screenshot(fileName:note:)`. On drain, `ConvexCaptureSink.saveScreenshot` (`ConvexCaptureSink.swift:65-74`) sniffs the format from bytes (`Capture/ImageFormat.swift:12-30` — PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/HEIC magic), POSTs to `captures:generateUploadUrl`, then `captures:createCapture` with `screenshotId`. Extraction happens server-side and is not visible from iOS.

> **Finding — a dropped field.** `QueuedCapture.Screenshot` carries `note` (`CaptureQueue.swift:38`) and `ShareSheetModel.capture` populates it (`ShareSheetModel.swift:281-283`), but the drain's screenshot branch (`CaptureDrain.swift:162-182`) calls `sink.saveScreenshot(image)` only, and `CaptureSink.saveScreenshot` takes no note (`CaptureDrain.swift:27`). **A note typed on a screenshot share is written to disk and then silently discarded.** Profile and manual captures carry theirs through.

## 5. Capture pipeline (client side)

A "capture" is a `QueuedCapture{id: UUID, capturedAt: Date, payload}` on disk (`Shared/CaptureQueue.swift:8-106`). Three payloads:

- **`.profile`** (`:21-32`) — `link: ProfileLink{platform, handle}`, `profileUrl`, `name`, `note?`, `attachToPersonId?`.
- **`.screenshot`** (`:36-39`) — `fileName`, `note?`.
- **`.manual`** (`:47-105`) — `name`, `platform` (free-form string), `handleValue`, `profileUrl` (`""` when no web profile), `note?`, `attachToPersonId?`, `source?`, `platformId?`. Hand-written init because Swift drops defaulted `let`s from the memberwise init (`:80-95`).

Producers: `ShareSheetModel.capture` (share extension + pin walkthrough), `AddPersonDraft.capture` (`Directory/AddPersonDraft.swift:137-160`, `source: "typed"`), `ContactImportMatching.capture` (`Contacts/ContactImportMatching.swift:68-99`, `source: "imported"`).

**Wire shape.** `ConvexCaptureSink.saveShared` (`:76-128`) sends `platform`, `handleValue`, `profileUrl`, `name`, and — **only when present, never as explicit null** (`:118-123`) — `note`, `attachToPersonId`, `source`, `platformId`. Phone handles are normalized to E.164 here and only here, because the extension has no PhoneNumberKit (`:52-53`).

**platformId resolution** happens *before* the save, not after (`:94-99`, `PlatformIdResolving.swift:10-16`): the server looks handles up id-first, so resolving late would attach a rename to a twin instead of the existing person. Instagram: one unauthenticated GET to `i.instagram.com/api/v1/users/web_profile_info` with a public `x-ig-app-id` (`PlatformIdResolving.swift:99-117`), 5s timeout, defensive decode that accepts the id as string *or* number (`:50-63`). X: `composio:resolveXUsername` (`:119-131`). Both are best-effort and can never fail or delay the save.

**Outcome codes handled**

| Code | Where | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `status == "conflict"` | `ConflictRetry.shouldRetry` (`CaptureDrain.swift:42-44`) | one resubmit with attach stripped |
| `noteTruncated` | `CaptureDrain.swift:133, 152` | counted in `DrainResult.truncatedNotes`, **no UI** (`:74-86`) |
| `handleDropped` (8-handle cap) | `CaptureDrain.swift:134, 153, 195-197` | `os.Logger` breadcrumb only, **no UI** (`:113-117`) |
| `status == "handle_taken"` | `EditPersonOutcome` custom decoder (`PersonModel.swift:182-205`) | inline "That handle is saved on X" with form left open (`PersonFieldEditors.swift:298-306`) |
| `status == "already"` | `ConnectOutcome.wasAlready` (`ConnectModel.swift:42`) | treated as success |
| `status == "claimed"` | `HandleClaim.isClaimed` (`MyCardModel.swift:16`) | otherwise "taken" + server suggestions |
| `notConnected` (disconnect) | `PersonModel.disconnect()` (`:426-444`) | idempotent, treated as done |
| Composio `redirect`/`already`/`unsupported_account`/`failed`/`connected` | `ContactConnector.map` / `.step` (`:110-142`) | pure, unit-tested |

**Dedup** is server-owned on `(platform, handleValue)`; the client mirrors the fold in `MirrorHandle.valueKey` (drop leading `@`, lowercase) so the sheet never offers an attach the server will refuse. Re-entrant drains are safe because `saveSharedProfile` is idempotent and `CaptureSync` guards with `isRunning` (`CaptureSync.swift:84-86`).
