## 8. Data Storage and Synchronization

Local (iOS): the capture queue (one JSON file per capture + copied images) and `directory-mirror.json` (id/name/handles only, 500-person window) in the App Group container; UserDefaults flags (onboarding skip, promo dismissals, contact-suggestion state) keyed by user id; Clerk session token in the Keychain (SDK-owned).
Web local: exactly one localStorage key, `haven:hasSession` (splash hint).
Remote: everything else - Convex is the sole source of truth (`DirectoryMirror.swift:48-54` says the mirror is "a cache, never truth").
Sync: live Convex subscriptions on every read screen; the queue drains on launch/foreground; the mirror refreshes after every drain.
Conflicts: last-write-wins; the one explicit conflict protocol is capture attach (`conflict` -> one resubmit without the attach); `contactHandles` are rewritten wholesale on edit, with client-side carry-forward of platformId/source/addedAt to avoid metadata wipe (`PersonFieldEditors.swift:381-393`).
Offline: all four capture paths work fully offline; every read degrades to an "unreachable / try again" state; writes are 12s-bounded.
Deletion propagation: deletePerson cascades in one transaction; account deletion is a paginated self-rescheduling purge (200 rows/table/transaction) that also freezes rows in other users' directories; sign-out wipes the local queue and mirror (documented deliberate data loss, `LocalAccountState.swift:15-28`).
Migrations: no framework; Convex schema evolves additively with optional fields plus five hand-run internal backfill mutations (`backfillNormalizedNames`, `backfillSearchText`, `backfillPersonHandles`, `backfillLegacyHandles`, `backfillPhoneHandleKeys`).
Multi-device: works by construction (server truth + live queries); per-device queues never sync to each other (fine, they drain to the server).
Storage pressure: no evidence of concern at current scale; known ceilings are the 2000-row `listPersonNames` pool and the 1000-row `directoryFacets` scan, both documented.

## 9. Privacy and Security

- Authentication: **Implemented** (Clerk on all three surfaces; templated JWT on iOS; `auth.config.ts` fails loudly if unconfigured).
- Authorization: **Implemented and strong.** Exactly two intentionally public functions (`profiles.getByHandle`, `waitlist.joinWaitlist`) plus auth-optional `stripe.hasProAccess` (fails closed) and the signature-verified Stripe webhook; every other public function calls `requireUser` first (verified exhaustively); ownership mismatch reads as not-found (no existence oracle).
- Per-user isolation: **Implemented.** userId-leading indexes everywhere; vector/search indexes filter on userId; explicit cross-tenant guards with redacted logging in `oldestLiveOwner` and `mergeHandleIntoOwner` (`convex/people.ts:346-397, 476-524`); Composio account ownership proven by listing the caller's own accounts rather than trusting response fields.
- Row-level security: N/A as a database feature - Convex has no RLS; isolation is application-layer only (relevant for Polygres later).
- Encryption in transit: **Implemented** (HTTPS/WSS throughout; CSP-pinned origins).
- Encryption at rest: **Configured externally, not verifiable** (Convex-managed); nothing app-level.
- End-to-end encryption: **Missing.** No client-side crypto anywhere; all notes, handles, and screenshots are operator-readable plaintext. Marketing note: the codebase never claims "encrypted" - correct restraint; but any future "zero knowledge"/"local" claim for the iPhone app would be misleading today. The Sky page's "never leaves your Mac" claims apply to the separate Mac tool and are accurate for it.
- iOS Keychain: **Delegated** - only the Clerk SDK writes it; the entitlement exists solely for that.
- Secure Enclave / biometrics: **Missing.**
- App Group at rest: **Partial gap** - queue, screenshots, and mirror are plaintext with no explicit `NSFileProtection` class (default complete-until-first-unlock applies).
- Sensitive data in logs: **One confirmed leak** - `convex/waitlist.ts:87-100` logs raw signup emails on four paths; everything else is deliberately id-only, and iOS uses `privacy: .public` only on non-user data.
- Analytics/crash reports: **Missing by design**, enforced by CSP and verified against the privacy policy's "No analytics SDKs" claim; `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` declares no tracking. Consequence: zero field telemetry for a build heading to App Store.
- Model-provider exposure: **Implemented and large** - the ask call ships up to 200 dossiers of names, employers, cities, handles, and verbatim private notes (<= 120KB) to the configured provider; embeddings ship notes verbatim; extraction hands the provider a fetchable Convex storage URL to the raw screenshot. The privacy policy discloses an AI subprocessor (`src/LegalPage.tsx:109-127`).
- Backups: **Unknown** (Convex-managed; nothing in-repo).
- Account deletion: **Implemented end-to-end** (Section 2); `subscriptions` survives deliberately and this retention is **not disclosed** in the support/privacy copy.
- Data export: **Missing** entirely - the clearest GDPR/CCPA gap.
- Key recovery / multi-device keys: N/A (no E2EE).
- Other: waitlist rate limit is one global 40/min bucket (trivially floodable denial of signup, documented trade-off); `getByHandle` has no rate limit and handles are enumerable (3-24 chars `[a-z0-9_]`); `loveAlarm.nearby` is room-code-gated only (intended opt-in semantic); `captures.generateUploadUrl` and `acceptCapture` lack rate limits their siblings have (backend audit F3/F4); a personal Gmail address is hardcoded as the default admin allowlist entry (`src/lib.ts:74`); dev-tool `sync_polygres.py` pushes un-anonymized real phone numbers/emails/names into Polygres.

## 10. Current AI and Agent System

All inference is server-side in Convex actions via hand-rolled fetch against OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`convex/openaiClient.ts:132-152`); no SDK, no client-side inference, no streaming anywhere.
Provider routing: `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` defaults, with all-or-nothing `EXTRACTION_*` and `ASK_*` overrides (a custom base URL must bring its own key so the OpenAI bearer is never sent to a third party, `openaiClient.ts:112-118`).
Models: extraction and ask default `gpt-4o-mini`; embeddings hard-pinned `text-embedding-3-small` 1536-dim.
Structured output: strict `json_schema` on both chat features, `refusal` checked, plus server-side re-validation of every model-returned reference.
Fallback: none (no second provider, no model fallback).
Cost controls: per-user fixed-window rate limits on every spend path, including ask at 10/min + 100/day with an explicit "an ask costs ~100x a semantic search" rationale (`people.ts:2476-2490`), and a Composio-shared 50/day X-lookup cap.
Safety/grounding: the ask prompt forbids inventing people/facts/refs, distinguishes direct vs bridge, and demands a clarifying question over guessing; server drops unknown/duplicate refs and renders person fields from its own data, so injection cannot fabricate a person - but the free-form `why` string is unvalidated model output, and no injection fencing exists anywhere (Section 9).

**Feature 1 - screenshot extraction.**
User shares screenshot -> upload to Convex storage -> `createCapture` (rate-limited, image-validated) -> scheduled `internal.captures.extract` -> signed URL passed as `image_url` (detail: low) with the extraction prompt (`openaiClient.ts:60-72`) and `EXTRACTION_SCHEMA` -> parse + `is_profile`/name gate -> `finishExtract` stores `{platform, name, handle?, headline?, bio?}` on the capture -> user triages -> accept copies fields into a person -> memories + embeddings scheduled -> person searchable.
Errors: allowlisted user-safe message; raw detail server-only; user-initiated retry; 15-min stuck sweep.

**Feature 2 - ask my network (iOS).**
User question + client-held history (`AskModel.swift:104-144`) -> `people.ask` (`people.ts:2448-2574`): requireUser, rate limits, bounds (20 turns, 2000 chars) -> context assembly: up to 200 people newest-first with up to 12 memory lines each, built into numbered dossiers (`buildDossier`, `src/lib.ts:359-395`) under a 120k-char budget; only if the cap or budget truncated does it fall back to vector-ranking candidates (`rankPeopleForAsk`, no score floor) -> one chat call with the ask system prompt + `ASK_SCHEMA` -> server re-validates refs, caps 10 matches -> returns matches (kind direct|bridge, why, server-hydrated person fields) + optional clarifying question -> rendered in AskPanel.
Nothing is stored server-side; no retry on provider failure.

**Feature 3 - semantic search (web + iOS-adjacent).**
Query (>= 3 chars, 300ms debounce) -> `semanticSearch` action: requireUser, 30/min -> `embedText(term)` -> parallel vectorSearch over people (limit 8) and memories (limit 64), both userId-filtered, floor 0.3 -> best-score-per-person, memory wins ties, matching memory line attached as `evidence` -> top 8 hydrated.
Web renders only a "memory" tag; the `evidence` line is returned but never displayed (`SearchAdd.tsx`); failures are silently swallowed to an empty result.

**Feature 4 - graph/ name guessing (research tool, local-only).**
Ollama at localhost with ephemeral URLSession; real message snippets prompt-input but never persisted; strict grounding (tokens must appear in snippets); out of Haven's product path.

## 11. Memory Pipeline

Distinctions that exist today: raw source (screenshot blob + capture row), extracted structured fields (platform/name/handle/headline/bio - model output stored *unmarked* once accepted), the user's note (`people.context`), derived per-line `memories` rows, and the embedding layer.
Not represented: interactions, summaries, structured assertions, interests/traits/goals as data, model-generated inferences as a distinct class.

- Input -> processing: every write to `context` (add, edit, capture accept, shared-profile save) runs `syncMemories`: newline split, trim, exact-text dedup against existing rows, insert, schedule per-line embed (`memories.ts:38-88`).
- Model/algorithm: no LLM in the memory path itself - extraction is the only LLM writer, and only into person fields, not memories.
- Output/persistence: memory rows `{userId, personId, text, createdAt, embedding?, embeddedText?}`.
- Confidence: none anywhere.
- Provenance: partial - handles carry source (proven/typed/imported) and captures keep the screenshot; memory lines carry no source (user-typed vs capture-bio-derived is indistinguishable once in `context`).
- Deduplication: exact-text only; a rephrased duplicate creates a second row; `appendContext` has a verbatim-substring replay guard (`people.ts:556-576`).
- Contradiction handling: none - "moved to Berlin" and "lives in SF" coexist and both retrieve.
- Reprocessing: embeddings are idempotent on `embeddedText`; daily backfill crons (person-side cron is defective past 200 rows - F1).
- User correction: editing the note updates `context` and *adds* new lines but never removes old rows - the documented cost is "a typo fixed in the note leaves the typo'd line searchable" (`memories.ts:48-51`); the real cost is that redacted sensitive text stays retrievable in semantic search and ask dossiers until the person is deleted.
- Deletion: person deletion cascades memories + embeddings correctly; there is no per-memory deletion surface.

**Where an LLM inference becomes a "fact":** on capture accept, model-extracted `headline` and `bio` are copied into the person row indistinguishable from user-entered data, then flow into the search haystack, the embedding text, and ask dossiers.
The extraction prompt's anti-guessing clause is the only mitigation (`openaiClient.ts:66-72`).
The reserved-but-unwritten `"guessed"` handle source (`peopleFields.ts:12-18`) shows the team knows this class matters; nothing equivalent exists for text fields.

## 12. Search and Retrieval

Mechanisms in use: exact/prefix keyword search (Convex search indexes with accent-folding), structured chip equality (companyKey/cityKey/roleKey, index-backed), client-side fuzzy name matching (Levenshtein, web only), vector similarity (two indexes), and LLM retrieval-and-rank inside ask.
Not used: SQL, graph traversal, LLM-generated queries, reranking models, true hybrid fusion (keyword and semantic results render side by side on web but are never merged or cross-scored).

Natural-language handling: there is no query interpretation layer - a web query goes verbatim to both the name search index and (>= 3 chars) `embedText` for vector search; ask sends the raw question to the LLM with the dossier corpus and lets the model do interpretation, matching, and explanation in one call.
Permissions: userId filters at the index level everywhere; ask re-checks row ownership even on internally-derived ids.
Evidence: semanticSearch attaches the best-matching memory line (`evidence`, unrendered on web); ask requires a `why` per match and clarifies rather than guesses; keyword search returns no evidence (the match is implicit).

Representative examples grounded in current code:
1. `"maria"` -> `searchPeople` prefix-matches `normalizedName` (accent-insensitive, so "María" matches); results are directory rows; typo `"mria"` gets a web "Same person?" suggestion via Levenshtein over the 2000-name pool.
2. `company:LinkedIn city:SF` (iOS chips) -> `searchDirectory` ranges the most selective chip index and post-filters the rest (`people.ts:1077-1118`); counts come from `directoryFacets` (approximate past 1000 rows).
3. `"spain shirt party"` -> semanticSearch embeds the phrase, hits the memory line "wore the Spain jersey at Dario's party" at cosine >= 0.3, and returns that person with the line as evidence; the same need phrased as a question ("who was the guy in the Spain shirt?") only gets a grounded answer through iOS ask.

## 13. Matching and Recommendations

What "matching" means in the code today: (a) query-to-person and query-to-memory matching (Sections 12), and (b) LLM-judged need-to-person matching inside ask - `direct` ("the person themselves fits the need") vs `bridge` ("a plausible route to someone who does"), the embryo of introduction discovery.
Candidate generation for ask: recency (newest 200), vector rank only on overflow; scoring/ranking: entirely the model's, ordered "best first," padded matches forbidden; thresholds: none beyond the 10-match cap; evidence: the `why` string plus server-hydrated person fields; recency: implicit in candidate order; user feedback: none captured; consent: not applicable - matches are private to the asker, and no introduction mechanism exists.
Not implemented (aspirational only): people-to-people similarity, complementary needs/offers (no such fields exist), relationship-path traversal (no intra-directory person-to-person edges exist), cross-user suggestion, introductions, Love Alarm-based discovery (backend rooms exist; product surface absent).
The acquaintance-graph scoring that the vision needs exists - but in `graph/`, over iMessage metadata, for one user, outside Haven (`AcquaintanceScoring.swift`; tiers confirmed/strong/likely; "absence of an edge means no observed evidence").

## 14. Polygres Readiness Assessment

**This section is an architectural assessment, not an implementation plan.**
It follows the repo's own proposal (`docs/2026-07-31-polygres-network-design.md`, untracked, "Status: proposed, nothing applied") and the Polygres retrieval-design discipline (smallest sufficient strategy; filters are not an authorization boundary; bounded traversal; recorded embedding contract).

Compatibility findings:
- **Existing Postgres usage:** none in the app. The Polygres project (`pa6ee1830f10557dcc9bfd0c`, tier_nano) is provisioned with env names `DATABASE_URL`/`DIRECT_URL` staged in `.env.local.example`; today it contains only the graph tool's `im_nodes`/`im_edges` (684/1014 rows) - un-anonymized iMessage-derived identities, which is a charter contradiction to resolve before any app data lands beside them.
- **Node candidates:** `people`, `profiles`, `memories` map cleanly; Convex `_id` strings are stable, durable text primary keys (the design doc already plans exactly this). `personHandles` is better as node properties/an identity table than as nodes.
- **Edge candidates:** today only `connections` (user-to-user) and `memories.personId` (structural). The load-bearing gap: **no person-to-person edges exist within a directory**, so "graph retrieval" has almost nothing to traverse until either the acquaintance-graph edges migrate in (explicit charter change required) or a new intra-directory relationship entity is created.
- **Lexical:** `context`/memory lines, headline, bio, name, company, role are ready TSVector sources; the design doc's choice of the `simple` configuration (names must not be stemmed) is sound.
- **Vector:** embeddings already exist with a fully specified contract - text-embedding-3-small, 1536-dim, cosine, `embeddedText` as the idempotency key, `buildEmbedText` as the input template - directly portable to pgvector-style storage.
- **User isolation:** Convex enforces isolation in application code; Polygres retrieval must carry `user_id` as a mandatory predicate at candidate generation *and* at result resolution, per the "filters are not an authorization boundary" rule. The design doc's mitigation - Polygres is a server-side read model only, never read by UI - is the right containment.
- **Must never reach server-side retrieval:** `errorDetail`, Clerk token identifiers beyond the isolation key, other tenants' rows, and (pending a decision) the raw iMessage-derived tables.
- **Supernode risk:** low today (200-memory cap, 8-handle cap); future acquaintance edges and any company/city entity nodes are the classic high-degree hazards (the graph tool already caps fan-out at 20/node, depth <= 3, 200 rows - keep those bounds).
- **Migration complexity:** moderate - an incremental Convex->Polygres sync (the graph tool's `sync_polygres.py` is a working precedent, including the TRUNCATE-with-FK workaround), plus deletion propagation from `deletePerson`/`purgeOwnedRows` into the read model, which does not exist yet and is a hard correctness requirement.
- **Lock-in:** low on the data (plain Postgres shapes, standard embeddings), higher on retrieval configuration; Convex remains the system of record in the proposed shape, so rollback is "stop syncing."
- **Operational unknowns (from the design doc, still unresolved):** whether Convex `"use node"` actions can reach `*.api.db.polygres.com`; sync latency/freshness; Runtime API key management; the <500ms per-stage latency target unvalidated.

**Initial retrieval shape for "Find people I know who may be useful for an education startup":**
1. Query interpretation: LLM (the existing ask model) extracts structured intent - domain terms ("education", "edtech", "teacher", "school"), needed roles, and the asker's user_id (from auth, never the model).
2. Structured filters: relational `WHERE user_id = $me` always; optional chip predicates if the interpreter found any (e.g. role ILIKE patterns) - relational first, per strategy selection.
3. Lexical retrieval: TSVector (`simple` config) over memory lines + headline/bio/company/role for the domain terms; candidate cap ~100.
4. Vector retrieval: embed the need statement; top-k over memory vectors (k~64) and person vectors (k~16), same model/dimensions as stored, minimum-score floor to be calibrated (the current 0.3 is itself flagged for recalibration).
5. Graph expansion: from lexical+vector anchor people, one bounded hop over whatever edges exist (today: `connections` only; later: acquaintance edges), direction both, depth <= 2, fan-out <= 20, cycle-safe, to surface bridge candidates ("knows someone at an accelerator").
6. Reranking: merge by explicit rule (dedupe on person id; score = weighted lexical rank + vector score + graph proximity, exact-predicate hits boosted); or hand the merged candidate set to the LLM as ranked dossiers, as ask does today.
7. Evidence collection: carry provenance per candidate - strategy, source table, row id, matching memory line/TSVector headline, vector score, graph path - so every result can say *why*.
8. Response generation: the existing ask contract (direct vs bridge, `why` required, refs re-validated server-side against the shown set) already implements the right grounding discipline; reuse it.
Degraded modes must be explicit: if the vector index is unready, fall back to lexical + relational and say coverage is partial rather than silently narrowing semantics.

## 19. Technical Debt and Risks

Ranked by combined user/privacy/data-integrity impact and likelihood of blocking future work:
1. **Additive-only memories with no provenance or correction path** - user impact (redacted text stays retrievable), privacy impact, and the single biggest blocker to a serious retrieval/matching layer; moderate fix difficulty (needs a deletion/versioning design, then embedding cleanup). `memories.ts:48-51`.
2. **F1: embed-backfill blindness past 200 people** - silently unsearchable people; trivial fix (push the predicate into the index like `memories.ts:194-204`); high certainty. `people.ts:2578-2587`.
3. **Prompt injection with no fencing** - third-party bios and forged assistant turns reach the ask prompt; `why` is unvalidated output; medium fix (delimiting, role validation, output policy). Section 9/B10.
4. **LLM extractions become unmarked facts** - headline/bio enter search/embeddings/ask indistinguishable from user input; ties into risk 1.
5. **Privacy-promise fragility** - plaintext operator-readable data + large AI-provider payloads vs "private notebook" marketing; undisclosed subscription retention; waitlist emails in logs (`waitlist.ts:87-100`); missing export.
6. **Two person-edit contracts** (`updatePerson` clears-on-omit vs `editPerson`) - a web/iOS drift trap; low fix cost, real corruption potential.
7. **No field telemetry** - no crash reporting or analytics for an App Store submission; failures surface only as in-app "try again."
8. **Provider coupling** - embeddings hard-pinned to one model/dimension (re-embed migration to change); no model fallback; extraction currently dead demonstrates the single-point failure.
9. **Multiple truths at the edges** - directory mirror and queue are well-behaved caches, but `people.md` (real personal data, untracked, unignored) and the Polygres graph upload contradict the repo's own data-hygiene rules.
10. **No evaluation datasets in use** - `MIN_SEMANTIC_SCORE` uncalibrated; eval harness never run; retrieval changes are currently unfalsifiable.
11. Structural cleanups: memories lack an owner index (orphan unreachability, F2); missing rate limits on `captures.generateUploadUrl`/`acceptCapture` (F3/F4); global waitlist bucket (F5); error-type inconsistency (F7); vitest happy-dom docblock fragility.

## 21. Open Questions (founder-level, ranked by architectural impact)

1. What is the privacy promise, exactly - "access-controlled cloud with a disclosed AI subprocessor" (current reality) or something stronger - and does it permit server-side retrieval indexes (Polygres) over notes?
2. What counts as a memory: the free-text line as today, or structured assertions with source, time, and confidence - and must LLM-inferred attributes be visibly marked and user-confirmable before they influence search/matching?
3. Is Polygres strategic or experimental - and separately, do iMessage-derived acquaintance edges ever join Haven's data (an explicit charter change `docs/2026-07-31-polygres-network-design.md:26` says must come first)?
4. What is Haven allowed to infer at all (traits, relationships between saved people, "probably knows X"), and does inference require confirmation before becoming retrievable?
5. What information may feed matching, and do matches require *current* intent (a stated need) versus standing profile similarity?
6. May Haven ever suggest people outside the user's own directory (cross-user retrieval), which today is architecturally foreclosed and privacy-policy-contradicting?
7. Do introductions require consent from the introduced party, and what does the consent flow look like (the `connections` comment already leans mutual)?
8. Primary user and first use case: the founder-networker (app-store copy leans this way) or everyone-who-meets-people (README voice)? This decides whether needs/offers modeling matters at v1.
9. Data retention: how long do memories/embeddings live after edits and deletions; is the subscription-retention exception disclosed; when does export ship?
10. Cloud vs on-device processing: does any AI move on-device (the Sky tool proves local-model appetite), or is cloud LLM accepted permanently?
11. Business model: is the parked $4.99 Pro the plan, and what does it gate (ask volume is the obvious meter given the 100/day cap)?
12. Acceptable latency and cost per ask/search (the 100x-cost comment exists; no budget number does).
13. When does the one-tap connect become mutual-consent, and does the current write-into-peer's-directory behavior survive App Review scrutiny?

Input: current `memories`/`people` schema, the additive-design rationale (`memories.ts:38-51`), 5-10 real correction scenarios.

# Context to Give the Planning AI

**What Haven is.** Haven (repo `euno-app`, v0.48.0, branch `feat/identity-foundation` with large uncommitted changes) is a phone-first private relationship-memory app: a native SwiftUI iPhone app (iOS 18+, iPhone-only), a Convex backend with Clerk auth, and a React 19 web app on Vercel (inhavens.com). Tagline reality: "a private, searchable memory of everyone you know." The long-term vision (remember people, natural-language search, complementary-needs matching, grounded introductions) is documented in `mvp-design.md`, `todo.md`, and `docs/2026-07-31-polygres-network-design.md`; only the memory + search parts exist. A charter-separated macOS research tool in `graph/` ("Your Sky") builds a personal acquaintance graph from the owner's own iMessage metadata (confirmed/strong/likely edge tiers via shared-group and interaction scoring); it is distributed from the website as `YourSky.zip` despite its charter saying "never distributed," and its un-anonymized node/edge export (684 nodes, 1014 edges, real phones/emails/names) was already loaded into the Haven Polygres project even though the Polygres design doc marks that out of scope.

**What works today.** iOS: Clerk sign-up (Google/LinkedIn/X; Sign in with Apple removed, must return pre-submission); 3-question onboarding (name, city, one handle - optionally OAuth-verified via Composio with stable platformId + photo import); a generated "sky" card with claimable @handle and public web card at `inhavens.com/<handle>`; four fully-offline person-capture paths (manual add, share-extension for URLs/screenshots/vCards/plain text, Apple-contact import, QR connect that writes a person row into both users' directories with no accept step); one free-text note per person; live keyword search + company/city/role facet chips; iOS-only "ask my network" LLM Q&A returning direct and bridge matches with `why` strings; per-person reach links (X rename-proof id links, Instagram id deep links, LinkedIn 6-month staleness hint); edit/delete; full account deletion. Web: constellation "Atlas" search-and-add with a new Levenshtein "Same person?" duplicate suggester, semantic search, person detail/edit/delete, shared notes (connection-gated), screenshot capture triage (swipe deck), public card page, iOS waitlist. Stripe subscription mirroring exists but nothing reads it; Love Alarm proximity rooms exist backend-only.

**Architecture.** Convex is the sole backend: 13 tables, 84 functions, file storage, scheduler, 5 crons. No users table - Clerk `tokenIdentifier` string is the owner key on every row (`convex/authz.ts`). All model traffic is server-side plain fetch in `convex/openaiClient.ts` against OpenAI-compatible endpoints: gpt-4o-mini (default) for screenshot profile extraction (strict JSON schema, vision, detail:low) and for ask; embeddings hard-pinned to text-embedding-3-small, 1536-dim, with `embeddedText` as idempotency key. Env-based provider routing (`EXTRACTION_*`, `ASK_*` overrides). iOS holds a file-per-capture offline queue plus a 500-person `directory-mirror.json` cache in an App Group; the share extension makes zero network calls. Web deploys via Vercel; production builds also run `npx convex deploy`. CI: self-hosted Mac runner (vitest + xcodebuild), a daily Clerk-config monitor.

**Domain model.** `people` (per-owner person rows: name, free-text `context` note, capture provenance platform/handle/headline/bio/screenshot, structured city/company/role with fold-keys, up to 8 `contactHandles` each `{platform, value, platformId?, source: proven|typed|imported, addedAt}`, embedding); `memories` (derived, per-line rows split from `context`, own 1536-dim vectors, max 200/person, **additive: edits never delete rows - redacted text stays retrievable until the person is deleted**); `personHandles` (identity index: phone-aware valueKey fold + platformId, basis of all dedup); `connections` (binary mutual link, no pending state) + `sharedNotes`; `captures`; `profiles` (own card); `subscriptions` (webhook-only, survives account deletion); `waitlist`, `rateLimits`, `loveAlarmPresence`. Missing entirely: interactions, person-to-person edges within a directory, interests/skills/goals/needs/offers as data, introductions, confidence, per-field provenance for text. LLM-extracted headline/bio become unmarked "facts" on capture accept.

**Retrieval today.** Keyword: Convex search indexes over folded name and a haystack (name/headline/bio/company/role/city/handles/notes), userId-filtered. Chips: index-backed equality. Semantic: `semanticSearch` action embeds the query, runs dual vectorSearch (people limit 8, memories limit 64, floor 0.3 - flagged for recalibration), returns best-per-person with the matching memory line as `evidence` (returned but unrendered on web). Ask: up to 200 newest people as numbered dossiers (12 memory lines each, 120k-char budget; vector-ranking only on overflow) + strict-schema LLM call; server re-validates every returned ref against the shown set and hydrates person fields from its own data; matches capped at 10; client-held 20-turn history; 10/min + 100/day. No graph traversal, no reranker, no hybrid fusion. An eval harness (`scripts/eval-ask.ts` + `src/askFixtures.ts`) exists but has never been run against a live key - retrieval quality is unmeasured.

**Privacy model.** Strong app-layer isolation: every non-public function requires auth first; ownership checks everywhere; vector/search indexes filter userId; exactly two intentionally public endpoints (public card by handle - phone structurally excluded; waitlist join). No E2EE, no client crypto: all data is operator-readable plaintext on Convex. Large disclosed AI-provider exposure: ask ships up to 200 dossiers of names/employers/notes verbatim; extraction hands the provider a fetchable screenshot URL. Account deletion is a complete implemented cascade (subscriptions retained, undisclosed). Data export: missing (top compliance gap). No analytics or crash SDKs anywhere (enforced by CSP, declared in the privacy policy and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) - and therefore zero field telemetry. Known issues: waitlist logs raw emails; prompt injection unfenced (third-party bios reach the ask prompt; clients can forge assistant turns; only the `why` string escapes schema/ref validation); App Group files lack explicit NSFileProtection.

**Implementation status snapshot.** Working: auth (dev), onboarding, all capture paths, notes->memories->embeddings, keyword/chip/semantic search, ask (iOS), connect, public card, account deletion, offline queue, waitlist. Broken/dead: screenshot auto-extraction (dead API key in current env - manual naming is the de facto path); universal links (free Apple team, placeholder AASA team id - QR scans land in Safari). Unverified: production Clerk<->Convex pairing (nobody has signed in against prod). Known defects: embed-backfill cron goes blind past 200 people (`people.ts:2578-2587` JS-filters after `take(200)`); a note typed on a screenshot share is silently discarded on drain; two conflicting person-edit contracts (web `updatePerson` clears omitted fields, iOS `editPerson` does not).

**Confirmed technical decisions.** Convex-only backend for v1 (Polygres explicitly deferred as "the ambitious one," `mvp-design.md:71-76`); idempotent-outcome mutations (`{status: created|attached|already|conflict}`) with check-and-insert in one transaction; per-line memory rows with own vectors (retrieval granularity over correction); embeddings pinned (re-embed migration acknowledged); server-stateless ask; zero-network share extension with disk-queue API; platformId-first handle identity with provenance sources; web scope deliberately narrower than backend, enforced by a test; no analytics by design; prod deploy couples Convex to Vercel.

**Polygres state.** Project `pa6ee1830f10557dcc9bfd0c` (tier_nano) is provisioned; `DATABASE_URL`/`DIRECT_URL` names staged in `.env.local.example`; the untracked design doc proposes Convex-stays-source-of-truth + a server-side Polygres read model (UI never reads it), layered retrieval (relational exact predicates; TSVector `simple` config; vector reusing existing embeddings; graph traversal depth<=3 fan-out<=20 max 200 rows), Convex `_id` strings as text PKs, <500ms/stage target. Unresolved: Convex-action-to-Polygres connectivity, sync/deletion propagation (must mirror `deletePerson`/`purgeOwnedRows`), the fact that no person-to-person edges exist inside a directory (graph retrieval has nothing to traverse unless acquaintance edges migrate in - a charter decision), and the un-anonymized iMessage data already sitting in the project.

**Major constraints.** App Store: name reservation, Sign in with Apple, App Group/Associated Domains registration, paid team, prod Clerk verification - all external, all open (`todo.md`). Social platforms: no OAuth path for collecting others' handles (Composio verifies only your own); LinkedIn has no stable id (hence staleness hints); X integration unproven live. Apple: StoreKit must own iOS purchases (subscriptions.source is pre-shaped for "app_store"). Clerk issuer change orphans all rows (tokenIdentifier includes issuer).

**Most relevant paths.** `convex/schema.ts` (model + rationale), `convex/people.ts` (identity, search, ask), `convex/memories.ts`, `convex/openaiClient.ts` (all prompts/models), `convex/profiles.ts` (card, connect, deletion), `src/lib.ts` (routing, buildEmbedText, buildDossier - shared web/backend), `src/SearchAdd.tsx`, `ios/Haven/Shared/CaptureQueue.swift` + `ios/Haven/Capture/CaptureDrain.swift`, `ios/HavenShare/`, `mvp-design.md`, `todo.md`, `docs/2026-07-31-polygres-network-design.md`, `graph/PLAN.md` + `graph/GOAL.md` + `graph/JOURNAL.md`, `vercel.json`, `scripts/eval-ask.ts`.

**Highest-priority founder questions.** (1) The exact privacy promise, and whether it permits server-side retrieval indexes over notes. (2) What a memory is - free text vs structured assertions with source/time/confidence - and whether LLM inferences need marking and confirmation before they drive retrieval; plus correction/deletion semantics (today: additive, never deleted). (3) Polygres: strategic or experimental, and whether iMessage-derived edges ever join Haven (explicit charter change required first). (4) What Haven may infer, and what may feed matching; do matches require current intent. (5) Cross-user suggestion: today architecturally foreclosed and policy-contradicting - keep it that way? (6) Consent model for introductions and for the current no-accept one-tap connect. (7) Primary user/first use case (founder-networker vs everyone). (8) Retention and export timelines. (9) Business model (parked $4.99 Pro; ask volume is the natural meter). (10) Latency/cost budgets per ask and per search stage.

**Reading guidance for the planning AI.** Trust schema/code comments as design records (they are unusually deliberate), but not doc recency: README and several screen comments are stale, `PRODUCT.md` is self-superseded, CHANGELOG versions skip v0.44.0 and dates are non-monotonic.
